'''Blaine Williamson Gabbert''' (born October 15, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 13 seasons. He played [[college football]] for the [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri Tigers]], receiving second-team All-[[Big 12]] honors, and was selected 10th overall by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the [[2011 NFL draft]]. Gabbert began his career as the Jaguars' starter, but inconsistent play and injuries led to his departure after three seasons. He spent his next three seasons with the [[San Francisco 49ers]], where he saw his last significant playing time. For the remainder of his career, Gabbert served as backup for the [[Arizona Cardinals]], [[Tennessee Titans]], [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], and [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. As a backup, he won two [[Super Bowl]] titles, one with the Buccaneers and one with the Chiefs.

==Early life==
Gabbert was born in [[Ballwin, Missouri]], a suburb of [[St. Louis]]. He attended [[Parkway West High School (Ballwin, Missouri)|Parkway West High School]] in Ballwin, where he played for the Parkway West Longhorns [[high school football]] team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Steve |date=February 28, 2011 |title=Made for this: Blaine Gabbert has spent years preparing for the NFL |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nfl/news/179081-made-for-this-blaine-gabbert-has-spent-years-preparing-for-the-nfl |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121184302/http://www.sportingnews.com/nfl/news/179081-made-for-this-blaine-gabbert-has-spent-years-preparing-for-the-nfl |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 21, 2018 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=Sporting News }}</ref> He was a five-star blue-chip All-American and, according to ''[[Rivals.com]]'', was their No. 14 national player overall at any position. He was invited to participate in the [[Elite 11]] quarterback camp in the summer of 2007 where he won the camp MVP honors over [[Andrew Luck]] and then, in January 2008, he played in the [[All-American Bowl (high school football)|US Army All-American Game]].<ref name="Mutigers">{{Cite web |title=Blaine Gabbert |url=http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/gabbert_blaine00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228235146/http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/gabbert_blaine00.html |archive-date=December 28, 2014 |access-date=June 2, 2014 |website=Missouri Tigers Athletics}}</ref> He recorded 623 passing yards and five [[touchdown]]s as a senior, despite an injured foot that limited him to four games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stephens |first=Mitch |date=April 28, 2011 |title=Blaine Gabbert sticks up for Missouri recruits ahead of NFL Draft – MaxPreps |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/NyOPinFPEeCkhgAcxJSkrA/blaine-gabbert-sticks-up-for-missouri-recruits-ahead-of-nfl-draft.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825002713/http://www.maxpreps.com/news/NyOPinFPEeCkhgAcxJSkrA/blaine-gabbert-sticks-up-for-missouri-recruits-ahead-of-nfl-draft.htm |archive-date=August 25, 2018 |access-date=August 24, 2018 |website=MaxPreps.com |language=en-US}}</ref> As a junior, he posted 1,523 yards and 20 touchdowns (on 119-of-231 passing) and also added another 458 yards rushing and eight touchdowns. In his sophomore season, he threw for approximately 1,100 yards and 11 touchdowns as a first-year starter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Football recruiting database: Blaine Gabbert |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Blaine-Gabbert-55586 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005052945/http://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Blaine-Gabbert-55586 |archive-date=October 5, 2013 |access-date=October 4, 2013 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref>

==College career==
Coming out of high school in 2008, Gabbert was considered a major college recruitment prospect. Rated as a five-star recruit by ''Rivals.com'', Gabbert was listed as the highest ranked pro-style quarterback in the nation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 16, 2008 |title=Blaine Gabbert, 2008 Pro Style Quarterback |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2008/blaine-gabbert-13708 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155411/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2008/blaine-gabbert-13708 |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=October 14, 2022 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He initially gave a verbal commitment to [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]], but rethought his decision after head coach [[Bill Callahan (American football coach)|Bill Callahan]] was fired.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tucker |first=Billy |date=November 16, 2007 |title=Gabbert drawn by Mizzou's coaches |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/football/columns/story?columnist=tucker_billy&id=3113541 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155412/https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/football/columns/story?columnist=tucker_billy&id=3113541 |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=October 14, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He eventually committed to the [[University of Missouri]]. Missouri coach [[Gary Pinkel]] decided not to [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] Gabbert his freshman year, but instead play him as the third-string quarterback behind [[Chase Daniel]] and Chase Patton.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2008 |title=Missouri burns QB Gabbert's redshirt |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/college-football/article/2008-09-09/missouri-burns-qb-gabberts-redshirt |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090819153556/http://www.sportingnews.com/college-football/article/2008-09-09/missouri-burns-qb-gabberts-redshirt |archive-date=August 19, 2009 |access-date=August 16, 2009 |website=The Sporting News}}</ref> He saw action in five games in reserve duty, leading the Tiger offense to a touchdown against [[2008 Colorado Buffaloes football team|Colorado]] and a field goal against [[2008 Nevada Wolf Pack football team|Nevada]]. He completed 5-of-13 passing attempts for 43 yards and rushed six times for 22 yards.<ref name="Mutigers" />

Gabbert had a strong debut in 2009, throwing for 313 yards with three touchdowns in the air and another one on the ground against the [[2009 Illinois Fighting Illini football team|Illinois Fighting Illini]] in the annual [[Arch Rivalry]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Missouri vs Illinois Box Score, September 5, 2009 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2009-09-05-illinois.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121125921/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2009-09-05-illinois.html |archive-date=January 21, 2018 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He set career highs with 30 completions (30 for 51) and 468 yards against [[2009 Baylor Bears football team|Baylor]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baylor at Missouri Box Score, November 7, 2009 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2009-11-07-missouri.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121185905/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2009-11-07-missouri.html |archive-date=January 21, 2018 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The 468 yards were the second-best single-game mark in school history, second only to Jeff Handy's 480 yards against [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State]] in 1992. Gabbert was named to second–Team All-Big 12 honors by multiple league media outlets, and he was also granted honorable mention for all-league honors from the AP after ranking 2nd in the Big 12 (29th in the NCAA) in passing efficiency (140.45 rating). Gabbert ranked 4th in the Big 12 and 11th in the NCAA in total offense (292.08 avg.). He led the Big 12 with 8.1 passing yards per attempt.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 Big 12 Conference Leaders |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/conferences/big-12/2009-leaders.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180330012810/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/conferences/big-12/2009-leaders.html |archive-date=March 30, 2018 |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He achieved the 3rd-highest single-season passing total in school history, completing 262-of-445 passes for 3,593 yards, 24 touchdowns, and nine interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blaine Gabbert 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/blaine-gabbert-1/gamelog/2009/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121185901/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/blaine-gabbert-1/gamelog/2009/ |archive-date=January 21, 2018 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was also recognized for his success in the classroom and named to the 1st-Team Academic All-Big 12.<ref name="Mutigers" />

In 2010, Gabbert led Missouri to a season-opening 23–13 victory over [[2010 Illinois Fighting Illini football team|Illinois]]. He threw for 34 passes on 48 attempts, with 281 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2010 |title=Blaine Gabbert's second-half TDs rally Mizzou as defense stops Illinois |url=https://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=302470142 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155413/https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=302470142 |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=June 2, 2014 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Gabbert also went on to beat [[2010 Colorado Buffaloes football team|Colorado]] (17/29, 191, two touchdowns) despite being sidelined with an injury in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 9, 2010 |title=No. 24 Missouri fights off sluggish O, Blaine Gabbert injury to best Colorado |url=https://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=302820142 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155416/https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=302820142 |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=June 2, 2014 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Other highlights of the season include beating [[2010 Texas A&M Aggies football team|Texas A&M]] on the road (31/47, 361, three touchdowns),<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 16, 2010 |title=Missouri's defense stifles Texas A&M as Blaine Gabbert tosses 3 TDs |url=https://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=302890245 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155414/https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=302890245 |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=June 2, 2014 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> and upsetting #1 [[2010 Oklahoma Sooners football team|Oklahoma]] (30/42, 308, one touchdown). That victory ended a seven-game losing streak against the Sooners, going back to 1998.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 24, 2010 |title=No. 11 Missouri rides 16-point fourth past top-ranked Oklahoma |url=http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=302960142 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141025135809/http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=302960142 |archive-date=October 25, 2014 |access-date=June 2, 2014 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Overall, in his last season with the Tigers, he had 3,186 passing yards, 16 passing touchdowns, nine interceptions, 232 rushing yards, and five rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blaine Gabbert 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/blaine-gabbert-1/gamelog/2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121185927/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/blaine-gabbert-1/gamelog/2010 |archive-date=January 21, 2018 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
====2011 season====
[[File:Blaine Gabbert - Jacksonville Jaguars.jpg|thumb|200px|Gabbert in 2011]]
In January 2011, Gabbert announced that he would forgo his senior year to enter the [[2011 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laymance |first=Reid |date=January 3, 2011 |title=Blaine Gabbert entering 2011 draft |url=http://www.stltoday.com/sports/college/mizzou/article_8d5b9392-177a-11e0-bff5-0017a4a78c22.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155415/https://www.stltoday.com/sports/college/mizzou/article_8d5b9392-177a-11e0-bff5-0017a4a78c22.html |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=January 4, 2011 |website=St. Louis Post Dispatch}}</ref>

Gabbert was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the first round of the 2011 NFL draft with the 10th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412043957/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |archive-date=April 12, 2019 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Jacksonville traded up six spots with the [[Washington Redskins]] to select Gabbert.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 28, 2011 |title=Jags send two picks to 'Skins, draft QB Gabbert at No. 10 |url=http://www.nfl.com/draft/story/09000d5d81f8ccf2/article/jags-send-two-picks-to-redskins-draft-gabbert-with-10th-pick |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107065650/http://www.nfl.com/draft/story/09000d5d81f8ccf2/article/jags-send-two-picks-to-redskins-draft-gabbert-with-10th-pick |archive-date=November 7, 2012 |access-date=October 24, 2012 |website=[[National Football League]]}}</ref> He was the third quarterback to be selected that year, behind [[Cam Newton]] and [[Jake Locker]]. He is the only quarterback chosen in the first round of that draft class to win a Super Bowl.

On July 28, 2011, Gabbert officially signed his contract to play for the team. The deal was worth $12 million over four years.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 28, 2011 |title=Jacksonville Jaguars sign No. 10 overall pick Blaine Gabbert |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/6813872/jacksonville-jaguars-sign-no-10-overall-pick-blaine-gabbert |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107180519/http://espn.go.com/nfl/story/_/id/6813872/jacksonville-jaguars-sign-no-10-overall-pick-blaine-gabbert |archive-date=November 7, 2012 |access-date=October 24, 2012 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

Though not slated to serve as starting quarterback, Gabbert quickly earned playing time under head coach [[Jack Del Rio]] after [[David Garrard]] was released in the preseason and [[Luke McCown]] performed poorly in the first two games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 6, 2011 |title=Jaguars release QB Garrard days before opener |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/6936966/jacksonville-jaguars-release-david-garrard-days-opener |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825002659/http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/6936966/jacksonville-jaguars-release-david-garrard-days-opener |archive-date=August 25, 2018 |access-date=August 24, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Gabbert played in his first NFL regular season game on September 18, 2011, against the [[New York Jets]] in Week 2.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at New York Jets – September 18th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201109180nyj.htm |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was then named starter against the [[Carolina Panthers]] the following week.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dillon |first=Dennis |date=September 21, 2011 |title=Blaine Gabbert named Jaguars starter |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/199720-blaine-gabbert-named-jaguars-starter |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825002646/http://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/199720-blaine-gabbert-named-jaguars-starter |archive-date=August 25, 2018 |access-date=August 24, 2018 |website=Sporting News}}</ref> In Week 5, against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], Gabbert threw a 74-yard touchdown pass to [[Jason Hill (American football)|Jason Hill]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Jacksonville Jaguars – October 9th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110090jax.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155424/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110090jax.htm |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> At age 22, Gabbert became the youngest player in league history to start 14 games in a season. He played most of the season with a toe injury on his plant foot.<ref name="CBS Sports">{{Cite web |date=April 17, 2012 |title=Gabbert's rookie year was a nightmare, but he won't be a bust |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/story/18622075/gabberts-rookie-year-was-a-nightmare-but-he-wont-be-a-bust |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151125053225/http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/story/18622075/gabberts-rookie-year-was-a-nightmare-but-he-wont-be-a-bust |archive-date=November 25, 2015 |access-date=June 2, 2014 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref>

Gabbert struggled in his rookie season. He was sacked 40 times, the third most by any quarterback in the league. He also fumbled 14 times, most in the league by a quarterback.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Leaders and Leaderboards |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/leaders.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200331234501/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/leaders.htm |archive-date=March 31, 2020 |access-date=October 3, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> His 50.8% completion percentage was second-worst in the league for passers with more than 200 attempts (ahead of only [[Tim Tebow]]'s 46.5%). His 5.4 yards per attempt was last in the league among qualifying passers, as was his 65.4 [[passer rating]].<ref name="11passing">{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Passing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/passing.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825002805/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/passing.htm |archive-date=August 25, 2018 |access-date=October 3, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> ''[[Football Outsiders]]'' calculated that Gabbert's 2011 season was "the fifth worst season we've ever measured" in aggregate value.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schatz |first=Aaron |date=January 2, 2012 |title=Final 2011 DVOA Ratings |url=https://www.footballoutsiders.com/dvoa-ratings/2012/final-2011-dvoa-ratings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220603132111/https://www.footballoutsiders.com/dvoa-ratings/2012/final-2011-dvoa-ratings |archive-date=June 3, 2022 |access-date=October 14, 2022 |website=www.footballoutsiders.com |language=en}}</ref> Pete Prisco of CBSSports.com predicted that Gabbert's potential remained high, and that many of his struggles could be attributed to injuries and the unfavorable circumstances around him, including a rush-centered offense, a lack of talented quarterbacks ahead of him, and a weak receiving corps.<ref name="CBS Sports" />

Despite his strong performance, the Jaguars lost 26–23 in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Minnesota Vikings – September 9th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201209090min.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811183229/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201209090min.htm |archive-date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 3, a 22–17 victory over the [[Indianapolis Colts]], Gabbert threw a career-high 80-yard touchdown pass to [[Cecil Shorts]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Indianapolis Colts – September 23rd, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201209230clt.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155454/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201209230clt.htm |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=March 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Gabbert struggled in the following weeks, including a loss to the [[Chicago Bears]], in which he threw two interceptions and fumbled once. Both interceptions were returned for touchdowns and the Jaguars lost 41–3.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Jacksonville Jaguars – October 7th, 2012 ===San Francisco 49ers===

====2014 season====
Gabbert was traded to the [[San Francisco 49ers]] on March 11, 2014, for a sixth-round draft pick. Coach [[Jim Harbaugh]] made the following remarks about Gabbert joining the team:
"I think he's a very talented player and his career so far hasn't gone on to be what he expected, and maybe others expected it to be. But I believe it can be a really powerful opportunity, powerful motivator for a player to say, 'It wasn't me, it was my situation.' And now he has that opportunity".<ref name="Niners Nation">{{Cite web |last=Fucillo |first=David |date=March 24, 2014 |title=Jim Harbaugh with some interesting comments about Alex Smith, Blaine Gabbert |url=http://www.ninersnation.com/2014/3/24/5542894/jim-harbaugh-alex-smith-blaine-gabbert-comments-2011-nfl-draft |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140605051926/http://www.ninersnation.com/2014/3/24/5542894/jim-harbaugh-alex-smith-blaine-gabbert-comments-2011-nfl-draft |archive-date=June 5, 2014 |access-date=June 2, 2014 |website=Niners Nation}}</ref>

Gabbert made his 49ers regular-season debut on October 19, 2014, during the team's 42–17 loss to the [[Denver Broncos]] in Week 7. He completed three of seven passes for 38 yards and a touchdown in his only appearance in the 2014 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Denver Broncos – October 19th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201410190den.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417032444/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201410190den.htm |archive-date=April 17, 2020 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2015 season====
[[File:Gabbert, Blaine.jpeg|thumb|225px|Gabbert in 2015]]
On March 10, 2015, the 49ers re-signed Gabbert to a two-year, $2 million deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=March 11, 2015 |title=On a day of amazing deals, the 49ers keep Blaine Gabbert |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/03/10/on-a-day-of-amazing-deals-the-49ers-keep-blaine-gabbert/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201129203808/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/03/10/on-a-day-of-amazing-deals-the-49ers-keep-blaine-gabbert/ |archive-date=November 29, 2020 |access-date=March 8, 2021 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref> Going into the 2015 season, he had a new head coach in [[Jim Tomsula]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pelissero |first=Tom |author-link=Tom Pelissero |date=January 14, 2015 |title=Jim Tomsula named San Francisco 49ers head coach |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/49ers/2015/01/14/jim-tomsula-san-francisco-49ers-new-head-coach/21773955/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825011159/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/49ers/2015/01/14/jim-tomsula-san-francisco-49ers-new-head-coach/21773955/ |archive-date=August 25, 2018 |access-date=August 24, 2018 |website=USA TODAY |language=en}}</ref> On November 2, 2015, he was named starter for the 49ers after [[Colin Kaepernick]] was benched.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wesseling |first=Chris |date=November 2, 2015 |title=Niners bench Colin Kaepernick; Blaine Gabbert to start |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/niners-bench-colin-kaepernick-blaine-gabbert-to-start-0ap3000000572076 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160101121451/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000572076/article/niners-bench-colin-kaepernick-blaine-gabbert-to-start |archive-date=January 1, 2016 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=NFL.com |language=en}}</ref> Gabbert made his first start since October 2013 on November 8, 2015, leading the 49ers to a 17–16 victory over the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. He completed 15 of 25 passes for 185 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions.<ref name="GAbbert">{{Cite web |date=November 9, 2015 |title=Teammates praise Gabbert while coach non-committal on another start |url=http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/story/san-francisco-49ers-blaine-gabbert-praise-from-teammates-110915 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151109085410/http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/story/san-francisco-49ers-blaine-gabbert-praise-from-teammates-110915 |archive-date=November 9, 2015 |access-date=November 9, 2015 |website=FOX Sports}}</ref> The following day, the 49ers announced that Gabbert would remain the starter when the team played the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on November 22. The 49ers lost 29–13, with Gabbert completing 22 of 34 passes for 264 yards and a touchdown with a 98.2 passer rating.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks – November 22nd, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511220sea.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121184459/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511220sea.htm |archive-date=January 21, 2018 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> With the 49ers down 20–13 against the Bears late in the fourth quarter on December 6, 2015, Gabbert rushed for a 44-yard touchdown, the first rushing touchdown of his career. He then threw a 71-yard game-winning touchdown to [[Torrey Smith]] in overtime for a 26–20 49ers victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seligman |first=Andrew |date=December 6, 2015 |title=Blaine Gabbert leads 49ers past Bears 26–20 in OT |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/blaine-gabbert-leads-49ers-past-bears-26-20-224400649--nfl.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208175317/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/blaine-gabbert-leads-49ers-past-bears-26-20-224400649--nfl.html |archive-date=December 8, 2015 |access-date=December 8, 2015 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> Gabbert finished the 2015 season with 2,031 passing yards with ten touchdowns and seven interceptions for an 86.2 passer rating. In eight games as a starter, he had a 3–5 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blaine Gabbert 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GabbBl00/gamelog/2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121184523/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GabbBl00/gamelog/2015 |archive-date=January 21, 2018 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2016 season====
On September 3, 2016, Gabbert was named the starting quarterback for the season opener.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=September 3, 2016 |title=49ers name Gabbert starting quarterback, make two trades |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2016/09/03/49ers-name-gabbert-starting-quarterback-make-two-trades/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155623/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2016/09/03/49ers-name-gabbert-starting-quarterback-make-two-trades/ |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=September 3, 2016 |website=ProFootballTalk.com}}</ref> After starting the first five games of the season, he went 1–4 which led to their coach, [[Chip Kelly]], starting Colin Kaepernick.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maiocco |first=Matt |date=October 11, 2016 |title=49ERS QB GABBERT RESPONDS TO BENCHING: 'IT SUCKS; I DON'T LIKE IT' |url=http://www.csnbayarea.com/49ers/49ers-qb-gabbert-responds-benching-it-sucks-i-dont-it |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161012024516/http://www.csnbayarea.com/49ers/49ers-qb-gabbert-responds-benching-it-sucks-i-dont-it |archive-date=October 12, 2016 |access-date=October 11, 2016 |website=csnbayarea.com}}</ref> Later in the season, he temporarily replaced Kaepernick. After a poor performance in Week 12, he was benched again. He was replaced by [[Christian Ponder]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Maiocco |first=Matt |date=December 18, 2016 |title=49ers inactives: Ponder replaces Gabbert as backup QB |work=NBCS Bay Area |url=http://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/49ers/49ers-inactives-ponder-replaces-gabbert-backup-qb |url-status=live |access-date=January 21, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180122001040/http://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/49ers/49ers-inactives-ponder-replaces-gabbert-backup-qb |archive-date=January 22, 2018}}</ref> Overall, in the 2016 season, he finished with 925 passing yards, five passing touchdowns, and six interceptions to go along with 173 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blaine Gabbert 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GabbBl00/gamelog/2016 |access-date=January 21, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
[[File:Blaine Gabbert 2017.jpg|thumb|175px|Gabbert in 2017|left]]

He was named the Week 11 starter after Palmer and Stanton suffered injuries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bergman |first=Jeremy |date=November 17, 2017 |title=Blaine Gabbert will start at QB for Cardinals vs. |access-date=November 19, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> During the game, Gabbert threw for 257 yards and a career-high three touchdowns as the Cardinals lost to the [[Houston Texans]] by a score of 31–21.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 19, 2017 |title=Cardinals come up short against Texans, 31–21, despite Blaine Gabbert's career-high 3 TDs |access-date=November 19, 2017 |website=Newsday.com |agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> Gabbert was benched on December 18, 2017, as the Cardinals' starting quarterback in favor of Stanton after not |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
[[File:Blaine Gabbert 2018 08-09.jpg|thumb|Gabbert in 2018]]
On March 27, 2018, Gabbert signed a two-year contract with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=March 27, 2018 |title=Titans Agree to Terms with QB Blaine Gabbert |url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Agree-to-Terms-with-QB-Blaine-Gabbert/8e9b6ff2-8645-4ce5-94a7-2618520ce0bc |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180327173439/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Agree-to-Terms-with-QB-Blaine-Gabbert/8e9b6ff2-8645-4ce5-94a7-2618520ce0bc |archive-date=March 27, 2018 |access-date=March 27, 2018 |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref> On September 9, 2018, in the season-opener against the [[Miami Dolphins]], Gabbert entered the game after starter [[Marcus Mariota]] suffered an elbow injury, but lost the game 27–20.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Miami Dolphins – September 9th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809090mia.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180920234806/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809090mia.htm |archive-date=September 20, 2018 |access-date=September 20, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Due to Mariota's injury, Gabbert started the following game against the Texans defeating them 20–17.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Tennessee Titans – September 16th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809160oti.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180920235056/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809160oti.htm |archive-date=September 20, 2018 |access-date=September 20, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Gabbert also started in Week 3 against his former team, the Jaguars. During that game, he struggled and was limited to eight passing yards before leaving the 9–6 road victory with a concussion.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 23, 2018 |title=Titans' Blaine Gabbert: Concussion confirmed |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/titans-blaine-gabbert-concussion-confirmed/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155513/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/titans-blaine-gabbert-concussion-confirmed/ |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=October 3, 2018 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> Due to another injury to Mariota, Gabbert started the final game of the 2018 season with a Wild Card playoff spot on the line.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=December 30, 2018 |title=Titans QB Marcus Mariota Inactive; Blaine Gabbert to Start vs. Colts |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-qb-marcus-marcus-inactive-blaine-gabbert-to-start-vs-colts?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155441/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-qb-marcus-marcus-inactive-blaine-gabbert-to-start-vs-colts?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=January 23, 2019 |website=www.titansonline.com |language=en-US}}</ref> In the game against the Colts, Gabbert passed for 165 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. The Titans lost 33–17 and missed the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2018 |title=Titans-Colts Postgame Notes |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-colts-postgame-notes |access-date=January 4, 2019 |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref>

Gabbert was released by the Titans on March 15, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teope |first=Herbie |date=March 15, 2019 |title=Titans trade for QB Ryan Tannehill, cut Blaine Gabbert |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001022882/article/titans-trade-for-dolphins-qb-ryan-tannehill-cut-blaine-gabbert |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190318021549/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001022882/article/titans-trade-for-dolphins-qb-ryan-tannehill-cut-blaine-gabbert |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 18, 2019 |access-date=June 26, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On March 27, 2019, Gabbert signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], reuniting him with head coach Arians.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vitali |first=Carmen |date=March 27, 2019 |title=Bucs Add Veteran Presence to Quarterback Room with Gabbert |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-add-veteran-presence-to-quarterback-room-with-gabbert |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210418022937/https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-add-veteran-presence-to-quarterback-room-with-gabbert |archive-date=April 18, 2021 |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> On September 24, Gabbert was placed on injured reserve with a dislocated shoulder.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=September 24, 2019 |title=Bucs Put Blaine Gabbert on IR, Promote Patrick O'Connor |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/blaine-gabbert-injured-reserve-patrick-o-connor-active-roster-roster-move-week-4 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155437/https://www.buccaneers.com/news/blaine-gabbert-injured-reserve-patrick-o-connor-active-roster-roster-move-week-4 |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref>

Gabbert re-signed with the Buccaneers on a one-year contract on April 2, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=April 3, 2020 |title=Blaine Gabbert Gets Second Act with Bucs |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/blaine-gabbert-re-sign-bucs-free-agency |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155431/https://www.buccaneers.com/news/blaine-gabbert-re-sign-bucs-free-agency |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> On February 7, 2021, Gabbert served as backup quarterback behind [[Tom Brady]] in [[Super Bowl LV]], where they would go on to defeat the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] 31–9 giving Gabbert his first Super Bowl victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=February 7, 2021 |title=What we learned from Buccaneers win over Chiefs in Super Bowl LV |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/what-we-learned-from-buccaneers-win-over-chiefs-in-super-bowl-lv |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211110010206/https://www.nfl.com/news/what-we-learned-from-buccaneers-win-over-chiefs-in-super-bowl-lv |archive-date=November 10, 2021 |access-date=March 8, 2021 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

The Buccaneers re-signed Gabbert on May 10, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=May 10, 2021 |title=Buccaneers re-sign Blaine Gabbert, adding fourth QB to roster |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/buccaneers-re-sign-blaine-gabbert-adding-fourth-qb-to-roster |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210510200121/https://www.nfl.com/news/buccaneers-re-sign-blaine-gabbert-adding-fourth-qb-to-roster |archive-date=May 10, 2021 |access-date=May 10, 2021 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> The following April, the Buccaneers once again re-signed him.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=April 6, 2022 |title=Blaine Gabbert back with Bucs |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/blaine-gabbert-back-with-bucs |access-date=February 14, 2024 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

Gabbert remained Brady's backup in 2022 and made his only appearance of the season in Week 18 against the Falcons. In the game, Gabbert completed six passes for 29 yards and a touchdown to [[Russell Gage]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 20, 2023 |title=Buccaneers' Blaine Gabbert: Another quiet season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/buccaneers-blaine-gabbert-another-quiet-season/ |access-date=October 16, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
Gabbert signed with the Chiefs on April 19, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McMullen |first=Matt |date=April 20, 2023 |title=Five Things to Know About New Chiefs QB Blaine Gabbert |url=https://www.chiefs.com/news/five-things-to-know-about-new-chiefs-qb-blaine-gabbert |access-date=October 1, 2023 |website=Chiefs.com}}</ref> He started the regular season finale against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] after the Chiefs elected to rest [[Patrick Mahomes]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=January 3, 2024 |title=Chiefs will rest Patrick Mahomes in Week 18, Blaine Gabbert to start |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/chiefs-will-rest-patrick-mahomes-in-week-18-blaine-gabbert-to-start |access-date=January 28, 2024 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> In his first start since 2018, Gabbert completed 15 of 30 passes for 154 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception to go along with 46 rushing yards during the narrow 13–12 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 7, 2024 |title=Chiefs' Blaine Gabbert: Uninspiring in spot start Chiefs defeated his former team, the [[San Francisco 49ers]], 25–22 in overtime during [[Super Bowl LVIII]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maaddi |first=Rob |date=February 12, 2024 |title=Patrick Mahomes |access-date=February 14, 2024 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> His contract expired on March 13, 2024 and he became an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McMullen |first=Matt |date=March 11, 2024 |title=Free Agency Tracker: Here's a Look at Which Chiefs Will Be Unrestricted Free Agents |url=https://www.chiefs.com/news/free-agency-tracker-here-s-a-look-at-which-chiefs-will-be-unrestricted-free-agents |access-date=September 12, 2024 |website=Chiefs.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Gabbert enjoys deep-sea and fly fishing in his free time.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Liotta |first=Colin |date=June 13, 2020 |title=A look at the offseason fishing exploits of Blaine Gabbert |url=https://bucswire.usatoday.com/2020/06/13/a-look-at-the-offseason-fishing-exploits-of-blaine-gabbert/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014155514/https://bucswire.usatoday.com/2020/06/13/a-look-at-the-offseason-fishing-exploits-of-blaine-gabbert/ |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=March 8, 2021 |website=Bucs Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> He has two brothers. Tyler Gabbert, committed to Nebraska, like Blaine, only to decommit and commit to Missouri. He never played for the Tigers and transferred to UCF. His youngest brother is [[Brett Gabbert]], a quarterback who played for the [[Miami RedHawks football|Miami University RedHawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clark |first=Dave |date=December 5, 2023 |title=Miami RedHawks quarterback Brett Gabbert to return; Aveon Smith enters transfer portal |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/miami-redhawks-quarterback-brett-gabbert-073452322.html |access-date=April 2, 2024 |website=Yahoo! Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

On December 29, 2022, while riding jet skis, the Gabbert brothers helped save four individuals in the water near [[Davis Islands (Tampa)|Davis Islands]] and [[Peter O. Knight Airport]] after an emergency landing of a helicopter. Blaine says he saw what "looked like a crew boat in the water that had broken up in about four pieces and I vaguely remember seeing like two yellow life jackets." The three brothers checked it out and called 911. They helped three people out of the water and onto their jet skis. Arriving Tampa Bay police officers helped the fourth person out of the water. Buccaneers Coach [[Todd Bowles]] described the rescue as "outstanding".<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2022|agency=Associated Press |title=Blaine Gabbert helps rescue 4 after helicopter crash in Tampa: reports |url=https://www.news4jax.com/news/florida/2022/12/30/blaine-gabbert-helps-rescue-4-after-helicopter-crash-in-tampa-reports/ |access-date=December 30, 2022 |website=News4JAX |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Buccaneers quarterback Blaine Gabbert helped rescue family from a helicopter crash via Jet Ski |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2022/12/31/sport/blaine-gabbert-buccaneers-helicopter-jet-ski-rescue-spt-intl/index.html |date=December 31, 2022 |access-date=December 31, 2022 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref>

'''Blair White''' (born February 20, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). After playing [[college football]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]], he was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2010. He played for the Colts for two seasons from 2010 to 2011.

==Early life==
White attended [[Nouvel Catholic Central High School]] in Saginaw, Michigan. As a senior, he had 63 receptions for 800 yards and 10 [[touchdowns]]. He also was two-year starter at [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] on the [[basketball]] team and played [[baseball]] as a [[pitcher]] and [[first baseman]].

==College career==
At [[Michigan State University]], White joined the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Spartans]] as a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/111209aac.html|title=Blair White: From Walk-On To Star Receiver|access-date=2010-12-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170211080435/http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/111209aac.html|archive-date=2017-02-11|url-status=dead}}</ref> After seeing limited time as a freshman and sophomore, he started five of 13 games as a junior. He finished the season with a team leading 43 receptions for 659 yards and a touchdown. He was a second-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten]] selection by [[Phil Steele]]. As a senior, he started all 13 games and had 70 receptions for 990 yards and nine touchdowns. He was named first-team All-Big Ten by the coaches and second-team by the media.

White finished his college career with 18 starts in 40 games, 116 receptions for 1674 yards and 10 touchdowns. He also earned First-team [[Academic All-America]] honors and Academic All-Big Ten Honors all four years of his college career.

==Professional career==

===Rookie season===
White was signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on April 24, 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/saginaw/2010/04/nouvel_catholic_centrals_blair_1.html|title=Nouvel Catholic Central's Blair White signs with Indianapolis Colts after going unpicked in NFL draft|date=April 25, 2010|website=mlive}}</ref> After spending the first couple of weeks on the Colts [[practice squad]], he was promoted to the active roster on September 26, 2010 after an injury to [[Pierre Garçon]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.nfl.com/2010/09/26/colts-sign-wr-white-off-practice-squad/|title=Colts sign WR White off practice squad}}</ref> He scored his first NFL touchdown in his NFL debut on a pass from Colts quarterback [[Peyton Manning]] against the [[Denver Broncos]] on September 26, 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/saginaw/2010/09/blair_white_catches_td_pass_fr.html|title=Blair White catches TD pass from Peyton Manning in first NFL game for Indianapolis Colts|date=September 27, 2010|website=mlive}}</ref>
White finished the 2010 season with 36 receptions for 355 yards and five touchdowns.

===2011 season===
In 2011 Blair played in 7 games but was severely limited by back injuries. He recorded no receptions, returning 7 punts for 22 yards. He was waived following the [[2011 NFL season|2011 season]] on April 13, 2012.

He opted to leave the NFL at 25.

'''William Jesse Winn Jr.''' (born April 15, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State Broncos]]. He was considered one of the best defensive tackle prospects for the [[2012 NFL draft]] and was selected in the sixth round by the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>[http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=72530&draftyear=2012&genpos=DT NFL Draft Scout]</ref> He also played for the [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[Denver Broncos]] and [[Green Bay Packers]].

==Early life==
Winn attended [[Las Vegas High School]], graduating in 2007.

==College career==
Winn attended [[Boise State University]] from 2007 to 2011. Where he recorded 133 tackles and 16 sacks.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/billy-winn-1.html| title= Billy Winn College Stats|publisher= Sports reference}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
Winn was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the sixth round with the 205th overall pick of the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Winn had a strong rookie season with 26 tackles, one sack, and one interception.
[[File:Billy Winn 2015.jpg|175px|thumb|right|Winn with the Cleveland Browns in 2015]]

===Indianapolis Colts===
On September 11, 2015, Winn was traded to the [[Indianapolis Colts]] for a conditional 2017 draft pick. He was placed on season-ending injured reserve on December 21.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.colts.com/2015/12/21/indianapolis-colts-make-roster-moves-127/|title=Indianapolis Colts make roster moves|work=blogs.colts.com|date=December 21, 2015|access-date=December 21, 2015|archive-date=December 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222163913/http://blogs.colts.com/2015/12/21/indianapolis-colts-make-roster-moves-127/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
On July 31, 2016, Winn signed with the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-place-nt-phil-taylor-on-injured-reserve-sign-de-billy-winn-17388496|title=Broncos place NT Phil Taylor on injured reserve; sign DE Billy Winn|last=Mason|first=Andrew|work=denverbroncos.com|date=July 31, 2016|access-date=July 31, 2016}}</ref> His free agent contract is for one-year and $760,000.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/denver-broncos/billy-winn-10026/|title=Sportrac.com: Billy Winn contract|access-date=November 7, 2016|website=Sportrac.com}}</ref>

On May 3, 2017, Winn re-signed with the Broncos.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos re-sign defensive end Billy Winn, waive Bobby Richardson|url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-re-sign-defensive-end-Billy-Winn-waive-Bobby-Richardson/b4f612be-2858-433e-9d9e-802cde1377ec|author=Swanson, Ben|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=May 3, 2017|access-date=May 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170504011800/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-re-sign-defensive-end-Billy-Winn-waive-Bobby-Richardson/b4f612be-2858-433e-9d9e-802cde1377ec|archive-date=May 4, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He suffered a torn ACL in the Broncos first preseason game and was ruled out for the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos defensive end Billy Winn suffers torn ACL|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/08/11/broncos-defensive-end-billy-winn-suffers-torn-acl/|author=Gantt, Darin|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=August 11, 2017}}</ref>

On April 22, 2019, Winn re-signed with the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-dl-billy-winn-dl-mike-purcell-ol-jake-rodgers|title=Broncos sign DL Billy Winn, DL Mike Purcell, OL Jake Rodgers|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=April 22, 2019}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 4, 2019, with a triceps injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos sign running back Theo Riddick|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-running-back-theo-riddick|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=August 4, 2019}}</ref> On March 5, 2020, Winn was released by the Broncos.

===Green Bay Packers===
On September 16, 2020, Winn was signed the [[Green Bay Packers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-t-ryan-pope-and-dl-billy-winn-to-the-practice-squad| title= Packers sign Ryan Pope and Billy Winn to practice squad|website=Packers.com|date=September 16, 2020}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on September 26 for the team's week 3 game against the [[New Orleans Saints]], and reverted to the practice squad after the game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kruse |first1=Zach |title=Packers elevate DL Billy Winn from practice squad for Week 3 |url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/2020/09/26/packers-elevate-dl-billy-winn-from-practice-squad-for-week-3/ |work=USA Today |access-date=September 27, 2020 |date=September 26, 2020}}</ref> He was elevated again on October 5 for the week 4 game against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], and reverted to the practice squad again following the game.<ref>{{cite news |author=Kruse, Zach |title=Packers elevate DL Billy Winn, LB De'Jon Harris from practice squad for Week 4 |url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/2020/10/05/packers-elevate-dl-billy-winn-lb-dejon-harris-from-practice-squad-for-week-4/ |website=USA Today |date=October 5, 2020 |access-date=October 7, 2020}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 24.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 24, 2020 |title=Packers announce roster moves |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-moves-x8727 |access-date=2025-02-11 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on December 9, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 9, 2020 |title=Packers activate G Simon Stepaniak from reserve/non-football injury |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-activate-g-simon-stepaniak-from-reserve-non-football-injury |access-date=2025-02-11 |website=Packers.com}}</ref>

'''Blair Richard Walsh''' (born January 8, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[placekicker]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for six seasons, primarily with the [[Minnesota Vikings]]. Walsh played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]] and was selected by the Vikings in the sixth round of the [[2012 NFL draft]].

In his first year, Walsh set the NFL records for the most single-season [[field goal]]s of 50 or more yards and the highest field goal percentage by a rookie. He also earned [[Pro Bowl]] and first-team [[All-Pro]] honors. After missing a short game-winning kick during the 2015 playoffs, Walsh struggled the following season and was released from Minnesota. Walsh spent his last season with the [[Seattle Seahawks]].

==Early life==
[[file:Walsh Army Bowl.jpg|thumb|left|Walsh at the 2008 U.S. Army All-American Bowl]]
Walsh attended [[Cardinal Gibbons High School (Fort Lauderdale, Florida)|Cardinal Gibbons High School]] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]], and played football for coach Michael Morill as their [[Punter (football)|punter]] and [[placekicker]]. As a senior, he made 14 of 20 field goal attempts and 30 of 31 extra point attempts.  Twice he hit field goals from 59 yards.  Walsh also averaged 41 yards per punt and 69 yards per kickoff.  For his efforts, he was named to [[USA Today]]'s All-USA First-team Offense and noted as a top-5 kicker in the nation by [[ESPN.com]].<ref name=autogenerated1>{{Cite web |url=http://www.georgiadogs.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/walsh_blair00.html |title=Blair Walsh Bio - Georgia Official Athletic Site<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=April 29, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303211955/http://www.georgiadogs.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/walsh_blair00.html |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He also played in the 2008 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]].

==College career==
Walsh attended the [[University of Georgia]], where he was a placekicker for coach [[Mark Richt]]'s [[Georgia Bulldogs football]] team from 2008 to 2011. He was a standout player who amassed a number of significant kicking statistics for which he became known as the "Athens Assassin".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.citypages.com/news/instead-of-a-lynching-maybe-blair-walsh-should-just-stop-looking-down-7686717|title=Instead of a lynching, maybe Blair Walsh should just stop looking down|last1=Zurowski|first1=Cody|date=September 24, 2015|website=citypages.com|access-date=December 5, 2017}}</ref> During his time at Georgia, he made 4 field goals in a game three times. Twice he attempted a field goal from his long, 56 yards, and converted it once in a game against Coastal Carolina in his senior year. In all, Walsh made 184 of 185 PATs and 76 of 103 field goals. However, in his senior year, he made just 21 of 35 field goal attempts.<ref>[http://blogs.ajc.com/atlanta-georgia-sports/2012/09/16/ex-bulldog-kicker-walsh-perfect-as-a-pro/ Ex-Bulldog kicker Walsh perfect as a pro | AJC Sports News Now<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024073841/http://blogs.ajc.com/atlanta-georgia-sports/2012/09/16/ex-bulldog-kicker-walsh-perfect-as-a-pro/ |date=October 24, 2012 }}</ref> He also had two tackles and one fumble recovery to his credit.<ref name=autogenerated1 />

===Minnesota Vikings===
====2012 season====
[[file:Blair Walsh Vikings kicker in 2012.jpg|thumb|right|Walsh prepares for a kickoff in 2012]]

Walsh was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] with the fifth pick of the sixth round of the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> A priority acquisition for the Vikings, Walsh would take over kicking duties for the released [[Ryan Longwell]]. Through the first 11 weeks of the season, Walsh missed only one field goal and had another blocked. He was 6-for-6 with kicks over 50 yards and 21-for-21 on extra point attempts. On December 16, Walsh passed [[Randy Moss]] for the Vikings' franchise record in points scored by a rookie (119). In his best week of his rookie season, in a game against the [[St. Louis Rams]] in week 15, Walsh equalled the NFL record for field goals made from 50 yards or more with his eighth kick (a new team record); his three 50-yarders in the game was also a team record.<ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Craig |title=Long field goals put rookie kicker in record books |url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/vikings/183733971.html |work=Star Tribune |location=Minneapolis |date=December 16, 2012 |access-date=December 18, 2012 }}</ref> His 5 kicks also tied an NFL record for most field goals of 37 yards or more in a single game, 5, which only [[Chris Boniol]] equaled for the Cowboys in 1996 and [[Scott Norwood]] in 1988. The next week in a game against the Houston Texans on December 23, 2012, Walsh completed a 56-yard attempt, setting the NFL record for field goals over 50 yards in a season with his ninth 50+ yarder. The 56-yarder also tied the Vikings record of longest field goal set by [[Paul Edinger]] in 2005. It was broken by Greg Joseph with a walk-off 61-yard kick on December 24, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/blair-walsh-sets-nfl-record-for-50-yard-plus-field-goals-0ap1000000115304|title=Blair Walsh sets NFL record for 50-yard-plus field goals|work=[[National Football League]]|date=December 23, 2012|access-date=December 23, 2012}}</ref> [[file:Blair Walsh postgame interview.jpg|thumb|left|Walsh speaks with the media after a game-winner against the Packers.]]In the final game of the 2012 season, Walsh completed a 54-yard field goal to make himself 10/10 over 50 yards on the season. He was 3 points short of tying an NFL record for most points in a season by a rookie at 144, Walsh ended 2012 with 141 points for the Vikings; which is the team record.  His final regular season field goal allowed the Vikings to beat the Green Bay Packers 37–34 and earn a playoff berth. The field goal also tied the NFL record for most field goals by a rookie kicker at 35 with [[Ali Haji-Sheikh]] from 1983.

As reward for his standout rookie season, Walsh was selected for the NFC team in the [[2013 Pro Bowl]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Gregg |last=Rosenthal |title=2013 Pro Bowl roster analysis: NFC |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/2013-pro-bowl-roster-analysis-nfc-0ap1000000117397 |work=NFL.com |publisher=National Football League |date=December 26, 2012 |access-date=December 27, 2012 }}</ref> Walsh was also selected to the All-Pro 1st Team. He was named to the PFWA All-Rookie Team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2012.htm |access-date=2024-08-03 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2013 season====
In the 2013 season opener against the [[Detroit Lions]], Walsh tied the record for most consecutive 50 yard or more field goals with eleven, tying with [[Robbie Gould]] and [[Tony Zendejas]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Mayer|first=Larry|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bennett-rebounds-from-drop-with-impressive-TD/dfb1ecc3-8a0e-4a96-8ea8-ac029a6ffd18|title=Bennett rebounds from drop with impressive TD|publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]|date=September 8, 2013|access-date=September 8, 2013|quote=Gould has now made 11 straight field goals from 50 yards and beyond, tying the NFL record set by Tony Zendejas from 1988 to 1993. The Vikings' Blair Walsh also tied the mark Sunday.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130911180803/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bennett-rebounds-from-drop-with-impressive-TD/dfb1ecc3-8a0e-4a96-8ea8-ac029a6ffd18|archive-date=September 11, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>  Walsh broke the record three weeks later against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in [[NFL International Series#2013|London, England]] with his twelfth straight 50+ yard field goal. On November 24 against the [[Green Bay Packers]] Walsh hit four of four field goals and had five touchbacks off kickoffs; he was named NFC special teams player of the week.

====2015 season====
In July, Walsh signed a four-year contract extension worth up to $14 million, including $5.25 million guaranteed, making him one of the top-five highest-paid kickers in the NFL.<ref>{{cite web |first=Ben |last=Goessling |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/13322168/blair-walsh-minnesota-vikings-signs-contract-extension |publisher=ESPN |title=Kicker Blair Walsh gets contract extension from Vikings |date=July 26, 2015 |access-date=December 29, 2015}}</ref>  He struggled in the preseason, making only five of eleven field goal attempts.  Walsh missed a 36-yard field goal attempt in a 20–23 loss to the [[Denver Broncos]] in week 4.  He picked himself up by converting seventeen consecutive field goals from week 4 in Denver through week 10 in [[Oakland Raiders|Oakland]], where he missed a 53-yarder that ended his streak.  During this span, Walsh kicked back-to-back game-winning field goals: a 36-yarder against the [[Chicago Bears]] in week 8 and a 40-yarder in week 9 against the [[St. Louis Rams]] in overtime.  Walsh has made five out of five field goal attempts on two occasions: week 7 against the [[Detroit Lions]] and week 16 against the [[New York Giants]], including two 50+ yard field goals in each.  For his efforts after scoring 19 points in Minnesota's 49–17 win over the Giants, Walsh was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.startribune.com/blair-walsh-is-the-nfc-special-teams-player-of-the-week/363825141/ |publisher=Star Tribune |title=Blair Walsh named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week |first=Matt |last=Vensel |date=December 30, 2015 |access-date=December 30, 2015}}</ref>

In the Vikings' 20–13 win over the [[Green Bay Packers]] in week 17, Walsh converted both of his field goal attempts, giving him a total of 34 made field goals, the most among kickers in the [[2015 NFL season]].

In the Vikings' first playoff game since [[2012-13 NFL Playoffs|2013]] against the [[2015 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] on January 10, 2016, in a game played in freezing weather, Walsh was 3-for-3 on field goals before missing a game-winning 27-yard attempt in the fourth quarter with 26 seconds remaining. Walsh hooked the short attempt wide left, and the Vikings lost the game by a score of 10–9.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nfl-shutdown-corner/blair-walsh-hooks-short-field-goal--seahawks-survive-vs--vikings-211539612.html |title=Blair Walsh hooks short field goal; Seahawks survive vs. Vikings |last=Edholm |first=Eric |date=January 10, 2016 |publisher=Yahoo! Sports |access-date=January 10, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2016/01/10/seahawks-vikings-blair-walsh-field-goal-miss-video |title=Vikings K Blair Walsh misses potential game-winning 27-yard FG |publisher=Sports Illustrated |date=January 10, 2016 |access-date=January 10, 2016}}</ref>

====2016 season====
Walsh struggled through the first ten weeks of the 2016 season, missing four extra points along with four field goal attempts. He missed an extra point in a 26–20 Week 10 loss to the [[Washington Redskins]] which led to his release from the Vikings on November 15, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Release K Blair Walsh|url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Release-K-Blair-Walsh/bdfb330a-47cc-45b1-a2f1-57e56c54bf1f|date=November 15, 2016|website=Vikings.com|access-date=November 15, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161116022815/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Release-K-Blair-Walsh/bdfb330a-47cc-45b1-a2f1-57e56c54bf1f|archive-date=November 16, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings release kicker Blair Walsh, add Kai Forbath|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/vikings-release-kicker-blair-walsh-add-kai-forbath-0ap3000000740131|author=Sessler, Marc|date=November 15, 2016|website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
After his release from Minnesota, on February 9, 2017, Walsh signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign Kicker Blair Walsh|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/02/09/seahawks-sign-kicker-blair-walsh|author=Drovetto, Tony|website=Seahawks.com|date=February 9, 2017|access-date=February 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170215064724/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/02/09/seahawks-sign-kicker-blair-walsh|archive-date=February 15, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Walsh gained national attention during his second preseason game where the Seahawks beat the [[2017 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]], his former team, 20–13. He went 2-of-3 on field goals of over 50 yards and converted both extra point attempts during the game. After his two successful field goals, he was seen pointing at Vikings head coach [[Mike Zimmer]] and his former Viking teammates for being taunted and having profanity yelled at him during all of his extra points and field goals. At one point, [[Richard Sherman (American football)|Richard Sherman]] joined in to show his support and respect for his new teammate.<ref>{{cite web|last1=DiNitto|first1=Marcus|title=Blair Walsh, ex-Vikings teammates exchange taunts during game|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nfl/news/blair-walsh-seahawks-vikings-preseason-score-2016-playoff-game-missed-kick/a8qhdjv86y7811t4cclw2r4np|website=sportingnews.com|access-date=December 31, 2017|date=August 19, 2017|archive-date=January 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180105175540/http://www.sportingnews.com/nfl/news/blair-walsh-seahawks-vikings-preseason-score-2016-playoff-game-missed-kick/a8qhdjv86y7811t4cclw2r4np|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On September 10, 2017, in the season opening 17–9 loss to the [[2017 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]], Walsh converted three field goals in his Seahawks debut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100gnb.htm|title=Seattle Seahawks at Green Bay Packers - September 10, 2017|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=September 14, 2017}}</ref>

On November 5, 2017, Walsh was 12 of 13 on field goals and 16 of 17 on extra points before the game against the [[2017 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]] where Walsh missed three field goals in the first half. The Seahawks went on to lose 17–14.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Henderson|first1=Brady|title=Pete Carroll on Blair Walsh's missed FGs: 'I'm disappointed for him'|url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/21308363/seattle-seahawks-kicker-blair-walsh-misses-three-field-goals-loss|website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 12, 2018|date=November 6, 2017}}</ref>

On November 9, 2017, Walsh made two field goals and two extra points in a 22–16 win against the [[2017 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]].

On November 20, 2017, against the [[2017 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]], Walsh made three field goals before coming up a foot short on 52 yard game-tying field goal with 2 seconds left, and Seattle fell short in their comeback, 34–31.

On December 3, 2017, against the [[2017 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]], Walsh made a 46-yard field goal on the Seahawks' opening drive to make it 3–0 and made three extra points in a 24–10 win against the Eagles that pushed the Seahawks to 8–4 in the season.

On December 31, 2017, as the Seahawks were playing for a spot in the playoffs against the Arizona Cardinals, Walsh made a 49-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter. With less than a minute remaining, Walsh missed a field goal, costing the Seahawks the game 26–24. Earlier that day, the Atlanta Falcons had won their game against the Carolina Panthers, so even if Walsh had made the go-ahead kick, the Seahawks still would have missed the playoffs.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Arnold|first1=Geoffery C.|title=Seattle Seahawks eliminated from NFL playoffs, lose to Arizona Cardinals in heartbreaking fashion: Live updates recap |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/nfl/2017/12/seattle_seahawks_vs_arizona_ca_6.html |website=Oregon Live|access-date=December 31, 2017|date=January 23, 2026}}</ref>
[[File:Blair Walsh Thomas Morestead 2013 Pro Bowl.jpg|thumb|Blair Walsh kicks a field goal in the 2013 Pro Bowl.]]
Due to Walsh's unsatisfactory performance in the 2017 NFL season, the Seahawks signed former [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] place kicker [[Jason Myers]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Henderson |first=Brady |date=January 3, 2018 |title=Seahawks sign K Jason Myers, a potential replacement for Blair Walsh |url=http://www.espn.com/blog/seattle-seahawks/post/_/id/29133/seahawks-sign-k-jason-myers-a-potential-replacement-for-blair-walsh |access-date=March 15, 2018 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> ''[[The Seattle Times]]'' said, "The signing of Myers could be the first step in Seattle reshaping its kicking units in 2018."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Condotta |first=Bob |date=January 3, 2018 |title=Seahawks sign kicker Jason Myers as replacement candidate for Blair Walsh |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/seahawks-sign-kicker-jason-myers-as-replacement-candidate-for-blair-walsh/ |access-date=March 15, 2018 |work=The Seattle Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On August 24, 2019, Walsh signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons agree to terms with three players, including kicker Blair Walsh|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-agree-to-terms-with-three-players-including-kicker-blair-walsh|author=McFadden, Will|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=August 24, 2019}}</ref> He was waived by the Falcons on August 31, 2019, as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons 2019 roster announced|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-2019-roster-announced|author=McFadden, Will|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=August 31, 2019}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On January 11, 2021, the [[New Orleans Saints]] signed Walsh to their practice squad to serve as a reserve kicker in the event that incumbent kicker [[Wil Lutz]] was unable to perform during their postseason run.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Alper|first=Josh|date=January 11, 2021|title=Saints will sign Blair Walsh to practice squad|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/01/11/saints-will-sign-blair-walsh-to-practice-squad/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210111182958/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/01/11/saints-will-sign-blair-walsh-to-practice-squad/ |archive-date=January 11, 2021 |access-date=January 12, 2021|website=NBC Sports}}</ref> On January 13, 2021, Walsh was released,<ref>{{cite news |author=Just, Amie |title=Saints shuffle practice squad roster, release veterans K Blair Walsh, LS John Denney |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/article_437c1bf4-55f2-11eb-bb65-3fde4737e824.html |website=NOLA.com |date=January 13, 2021 |access-date=February 17, 2021}}</ref> but re-signed with the practice squad on January 16.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=January 16, 2021|title=Blair Walsh: Rejoins Saints' practice squad|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/blair-walsh-rejoins-saints-practice-squad/|access-date=2021-01-18|website=CBS Sports|language=en}}</ref> His practice squad contract with the team expired after the season on January 25, 2021.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=Kat_Terrell |author=Terrell, Katherine |title=On the transaction wire today: The contracts of John Denny, Tommylee Lewis, Cameron Tom and Blair Walsh expired, essentially meaning the Saints did not sign them to reserve/futures deals from the practice squad. Werner was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the first round of the [[2013 NFL draft]]. He is co-owner and sports director of the [[Berlin Thunder (ELF)|Berlin Thunder]] of the [[European League of Football]] (ELF). ==Early life== Werner grew up in the [[Berlin]] neighborhoods of [[Wedding (Berlin)|Wedding]] and [[Reinickendorf (locality)|Reinickendorf]].{{cite news |url=http://www.tagesspiegel.de/sport/football-hoffnung-bjoern-werner-berliner-mauer-vor-dem-durchbruch/7572716.html |title=Berliner Mauer vor dem Durchbruch |first=Axel |last=Gustke |date=December 31, 2012 |newspaper=[[Der Tagesspiegel]] |language=de}} He originally played for the [[Berlin Adler]], before attending [[Salisbury School]] in [[Salisbury, Connecticut]], as an [[exchange student]] in 2007, as part of an exchange program organized by [[Pat Steenberge]].{{cite news |url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/sonst/bjoern-werner-deutscher-nfl-profi-neu-bei-indianapolis-colts-a-896712.html |title=Football-Talent Björn Werner: Superheld made in Germany |newspaper=Spiegel |date=April 26, 2013 }} He had 54 tackles, including 24 for losses, 12 sacks and two fumble recoveries in just eight games, but returned to Germany for his junior year. In 2008, he played on the [[Germany national American football team|U-19 Germany national team]] against the [[Poland national American football team|Poland U-19]] squad in [[Będzin]], winning 67–0.{{citation needed|date=June 2013}} In 2009, Werner returned to Salisbury, and logged 57 tackles in seven games with three sacks, four forced fumbles and two blocked field goals as a senior. Despite having played [[high school football]] for only two years, Werner was regarded a three-star recruit and ranked the fifth overall prospect in the state of Connecticut by [[Rivals.com]].[https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-2444 Rivals.com Connecticut Postseason Top 10 2010] Werner chose FSU over [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]], [[Miami Hurricanes football|University of Miami]], and [[California Golden Bears football|California]], during a [[National Signing Day]] telecast on [[ESPN]].[http://espn.go.com/video/clip?id=4883512 From Germany To Florida State] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121111053523/http://espn.go.com/video/clip?id=4883512 |date=November 11, 2012 }} Over [[spring break]] 2010, Werner married his girlfriend Denise, whom he had met in tenth grade in Berlin.{{cite news |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/mehr-sport/nfl/bjoern-werner-im-american-football-28071334.bild.html |title=Der Plattmacher: Björn Werner haut Amerika um |newspaper=[[Bild Zeitung]] |date=January 12, 2013 }} ==College career== Werner enrolled in [[Florida State University]] in [[Tallahassee, Florida]], where he was a member of coach [[Jimbo Fisher]]'s [[Florida State Seminoles football]] team from 2010 through 2012. He appeared in all 14 games as a [[true freshman]], registering 20 tackles, including 6.0 tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks, as a backup of senior defensive end [[Markus White]]. In his sophomore season, he took over as starter at left defensive end, registered 37 tackles, including 25 solo stops, 11 tackles for loss and 7 sacks for a Florida State defense that ranked second in rushing defense, fourth in scoring defense and sixth in total defense. In his junior season, he had his best collegiate season. He registered 42 tackles, 30 solo stops, 18 tackles for loss and 13 sacks. '''Blake Bell''' (born August 7, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the fourth round of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]], where he received the nickname "'''Belldozer'''", a play on words due to his large frame,  running style, and blocking ability.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fornelli |first=Tom |date=May 2, 2015 |title=49ers select 'Belldozer' Blake Bell who rumbled for 40 TDs at Oklahoma |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/49ers-select-belldozer-blake-bell-who-rumbled-for-40-tds-at-oklahoma/ |access-date=February 14, 2024 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref>

==Early life==
Bell attended [[Bishop Carroll Catholic High School]] in [[Wichita, Kansas]], where he played as a [[quarterback]]. As a senior in 2009, he threw for 2,752 yards with 32 [[touchdowns]]. He was ranked as the sixth best pro-style quarterback recruit by [[Rivals.com]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Bell, 2010 Pro Style Quarterback, Oklahoma |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/blake-bell-7483?view=pv |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

He was selected by the [[Detroit Tigers]] in the 43rd round of the [[2010 Major League Baseball draft]], but did not sign with the team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chadwick |first=Joanna |date=June 10, 2010 |title=Tigers give Blake Bell a fallback plan |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/high-school/article1047273.html |access-date=February 14, 2024 |website=Kansas.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kersey |first=Jason |date=February 16, 2013 |title=Blake Bell hadn't played baseball in two years when the Detroit Tiger... |url=http://blog.newsok.com/ou/2012/11/21/blake-bell-hadnt-played-baseball-in-two-years-when-the-detroit-tigers-drafted-him/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216130828/http://blog.newsok.com/ou/2012/11/21/blake-bell-hadnt-played-baseball-in-two-years-when-the-detroit-tigers-drafted-him/ |archive-date=February 16, 2013 |website=NewsOK}}</ref>

==College career==
Bell accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Oklahoma]] and was [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] in 2010. In 2011, he was the backup quarterback to [[Landry Jones]], but appeared in the Sooners jumbo package, leading to 44 [[Rush (gridiron football)|rushing]] attempts for 171 yards and 13 [[touchdowns]]. As a passer, he completed one of four passes for eight yards and an [[interception]]. He was the MVP of the [[2011 Insight Bowl]] after rushing for 51 yards on 10 [[Carry (gridiron football)|carries]] with three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Insight Bowl: Oklahoma's Blake Bell steps in at critical times |url=http://archive.azcentral.com/arizonarepublic/sports/articles/20111231insight-bowl-oklahoma-blake-bell.html |website=azcentral.com}}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2012, he was again the backup to Jones and was used mostly in the [[jumbo package]]. He rushed for 201 yards on 60 attempts with 11 touchdowns and completed 9-of-16 passes for 107 yards.

As a junior in 2013, he appeared in 11 games out of 13 games (8 starts), missing the contest at [[Kansas State University]] and the [[2014 Sugar Bowl]]. He made 140 completions out of 233 attempts for 1,648 yards, 12 touchdowns and 5 interceptions.

As a senior in the spring of 2014, Bell was converted into a [[tight end]] after the emergence of redshirt freshman quarterback [[Trevor Knight]] in the [[2014 Sugar Bowl]]. He appeared in 9 games and was used mostly for blocking purposes, posting 16 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 214 yards and 4 touchdowns.

Bell was projected to be a fifth round draft pick.
