===San Francisco 49ers===

====2015====
Bell was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the fourth round (117th overall) of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He was the fifth tight end chosen in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/draft.htm |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>  On May 11, 2015, the 49ers signed him to a four-year, $2.78 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $505,132.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Blake Bell contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/minnesota-vikings/blake-bell-16843/ |access-date=December 21, 2017 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], Bell faced stiff competition for a roster spot against [[Vance McDonald]], [[Garrett Celek]], [[Xavier Grimble]], [[Derek Carrier]], [[Asante Cleveland]], and [[Rory Anderson]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: San Francisco 49ers' depth chart: 07/01/2015 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/173/SF |access-date=December 21, 2017 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Jim Tomsula]] named him the fourth tight end on the depth chart to begin his rookie season, behind [[Vernon Davis]], Vance McDonald, and Garrett Celek.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: San Francisco 49ers' depth chart: 10/01/2015 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/176/SF |access-date=December 21, 2017 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the 49ers' season-opening 20–3 victory over the [[Minnesota Vikings]]. The following week, he made his first career reception off a four-yard pass by quarterback [[Colin Kaepernick]] during the third quarter of a 43–18 loss to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Pittsburgh Steelers - September 20th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509200pit.htm |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On October 11, 2015, he earned his first career start after Davis was inactive due to a knee injury.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 11, 2013 |title=49ers without TE Vernon Davis, LB Ahmad Brooks at Giants |work=SanDiegoUnionTribune.com |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sdut-jags-te-julius-thomas-active-expected-to-make-2015oct11-story,amp.html |access-date=December 21, 2017}}</ref> Bell finished the 30–27 loss at the [[New York Giants]] with one reception for six yards. He was a healthy scratch in Weeks 7–8. On November 29, 2015, Bell caught three passes for a season-high 67 yards during a 19–13 loss to the [[Arizona Cardinals]]. He saw increased snaps in the Cardinals game after Garrett Celek left the game due to an ankle injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maiocco |first=Matt  |title=Inactives: 49ers' Kilgore, Armstrong set to debut vs Bears |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/49ers/inactives-49ers-kilgore-armstrong-set-debut-vs-bears%3famp |access-date=December 21, 2017 |website=NBCSports.com}}{{Dead link|date=October 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=49ers Tight End Celek Goes On Season-Ending Injured Reserve | website=CBS News - Sacramento | date=December 8, 2015 | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/49ers-tight-end-celek-goes-on-season-ending-injured-reserve/ | access-date=April 14, 2026}}</ref>

The next week, he had a season-high four receptions for 43 yards during a 24–14 loss to the [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. He finished his only season under offensive coordinator [[Geep Chryst]] with a total of 15 receptions for 186 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Bell 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BellBl00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2016====
Bell competed to maintain a roster spot under new head coach [[Chip Kelly]], competing against [[Garrett Celek]], [[Bruce Miller (American football)|Bruce Miller]], [[Rory Anderson]], and [[Je'Ron Hamm]]. He was named the second tight end on the 49ers' depth chart behind [[Vance McDonald]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: San Francisco 49ers' depth chart: 10/01/2016 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/188/SF |access-date=December 21, 2017 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On December 18, 2016, Bell caught one reception for a season-high 45 yards during a 41–13 loss at the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. Unfortunately, he left the first half of the game after suffering a shoulder injury and was placed on [[injured reserve]] the following day.<ref>{{cite web | title=49ers' Blake Bell: Moved to IR | website=CBS Sports | date=December 21, 2016 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/49ers-blake-bell-moved-to-ir/ | access-date=April 14, 2026}}</ref> He finished the {{NFL Year|2016}} season with only four receptions for 85 receiving yards in 13 games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 19, 2016 |title=49ers Place TE Blake Bell on IR, Announce Additional Roster Moves |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-place-te-blake-bell-on-ir-announce-additional-roster-moves-18303025 |access-date=April 14, 2026 |website=49ers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Bell 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BellBl00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2017====
Bell contended for a roster spot under new head coach [[Kyle Shanahan]], going up against [[George Kittle]], [[Logan Paulsen]], and [[Cole Hikutini]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: San Francisco 49ers' depth chart: 07/01/2017 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/197/SF |access-date=December 21, 2017 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On September 2, 2017, the San Francisco 49ers waived Bell.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 2, 2017 |title=49ers Cut Roster Down to 53 Players |url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Cut-Roster-Down-to-53-Players/ba6c27ba-9518-4510-8baa-2698a0dcba11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180302212729/http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Cut-Roster-Down-to-53-Players/ba6c27ba-9518-4510-8baa-2698a0dcba11 |archive-date=March 2, 2018 |website=49ers.com}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
[[File:Blake Bell (38373209001) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Bell with the Minnesota Vikings in 2017]]
On September 3, 2017, Bell was claimed off waivers by the Vikings.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2017 |title=Vikings Acquire TE Blake Bell, Sign 3 to Practice Squad |url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Acquire-TE-Blake-Bell-Sign-3-to-Practice-Squad/2705ae9b-1605-4d07-8530-cd5a9207560b |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128154256/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Acquire-TE-Blake-Bell-Sign-3-to-Practice-Squad/2705ae9b-1605-4d07-8530-cd5a9207560b |archive-date=January 28, 2018 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> He began the season as the third tight end on the roster, behind [[Kyle Rudolph]] and [[David Morgan II]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Minnesota Vikings' depth chart: 10/01/2017 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/197/SF |access-date=December 21, 2017 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

Bell made his Vikings' debut in their season-opening 29–19 victory over the [[New Orleans Saints]]. On October 1, 2017, he earned his first start with the Vikings and caught a 12-yard pass from quarterback [[Case Keenum]] during Minnesota's 14–7 loss to the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref name="2017gl" />

On December 10, 2017, Bell scored his first NFL points, catching a [[two-point conversion]] during a 31–24 loss against the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref name="2017gl">{{Cite web |title=Blake Bell 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BellBl00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On December 15, 2017, the Minnesota Vikings placed Bell on injured/reserve after he suffered a shoulder injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters, Craig |date=December 15, 2017 |title=Vikings Elevate Kyle Carter, Place Blake Bell on IR |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-elevate-kyle-carter-place-blake-bell-on-ir-19986582 |website=Vikings.com |access-date=November 24, 2018 |archive-date=November 25, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181125030854/https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-elevate-kyle-carter-place-blake-bell-on-ir-19986582 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On September 1, 2018, Bell was waived by the Vikings.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2018 |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves, Set Initial 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-announce-roster-moves-set-initial-53-man-roster |access-date=April 14, 2026 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On October 16, 2018, he signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Links |first=Zach |date=October 16, 2018 |title=Jaguars Place TE Niles Paul On IR |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2018/10/jaguars-place-niles-paul-ir |access-date=April 14, 2026 |website=Pro Football Rumors}}</ref> He appeared in 10 games (4 starts), tallying 8 receptions for 67 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Bell 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BellBl00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs (first stint)===
On April 2, 2019, Bell signed with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=April 2, 2019 |title=Chiefs sign tight end Blake Bell |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/04/02/chiefs-sign-tight-end-blake-bell/ |access-date=March 24, 2023 |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> Bell scored his first NFL touchdown on January 12, 2020, with an eight-yard touchdown reception in the fourth quarter of Kansas City's AFC Divisional Playoff win over the [[Houston Texans]]. The Chiefs advanced to [[Super Bowl LIV]] where they defeated Bell's former team the 49ers 31–20.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=February 2, 2020 |title=Chiefs rally once again to defeat 49ers, win SB LIV |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chiefs-rally-once-again-to-defeat-49ers-win-sb-liv-0ap3000001100762 |access-date=October 31, 2023 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Bell caught one pass for nine yards in the Super Bowl.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LIV – San Francisco 49ers vs. Kansas City Chiefs – February 2nd, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202002020kan.htm |access-date=October 31, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On April 7, 2020, Bell was signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]], to take over the blocking [[tight end]] role that [[Jason Witten]] had the previous season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archer |first=Todd |title=Cowboys adding Blake Bell for tight end depth |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28952399/cowboys-adding-blake-bell-tight-end-depth |access-date=April 2, 2020 |website=ESPN.com|date=March 25, 2020 }}</ref> After starter [[Blake Jarwin]] was lost for the year with an ACL injury suffered in the season opener against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Bell became the backup tight end behind [[Dalton Schultz]]. He appeared in 16 games, making 11 receptions for 110 yards and no touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Bell 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BellBl00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He started the seventh and eighth game, when the Cowboys employed a two tight end formation to provide extra passing protection.

===Kansas City Chiefs (second stint)===
On March 18, 2021, Bell signed with the Chiefs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 18, 2021 |title=Chiefs sign Blake Bell |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/chiefs-sign-blake-bell |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He was put on the Reserve/COVID-19 list on December 21, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teicher |first=Adam |date=December 21, 2021 |title=Kansas City Chiefs add Tyreek Hill, 6 others to reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/32918325/kansas-city-chiefs-add-tyreek-hill-reserve-covid-19-list-sources-say |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He was activated off the Reserve/COVID-19 list on December 24, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 25, 2021 |title=Blake Bell activated off Kansas City Chiefs COVID-19 list, punter Tommy Townsend added |url=https://www.kmbc.com/article/nfl-says-blake-bell-chiefs-tight-end-blake-bell-off-covid-list/38611999 |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=KMBC.com}}</ref>

Bell re-signed with the Chiefs on March 24, 2022, to a one-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sweeney |first=Pete |date=March 24, 2022 |title=Chiefs bring back tight end Blake Bell on a one-year deal |url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2022/3/24/22994654/chiefs-bring-back-tight-end-blake-bell-on-a-one-year-deal |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=Arrowhead Pride|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> Bell was placed on injured reserve on September 5, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Foote |first=Jordan |date=September 5, 2022 |title=Chiefs to Place TE Blake Bell on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/chiefs/news/kc-chiefs-to-place-tight-end-blake-bell-on-injured-reserve |access-date=March 24, 2023 |website=SI.com}}</ref> He was activated on December 23.

In the 2022 season, Bell recorded his first career receiving touchdown in the regular season in the Chiefs' Week 17 game against the [[Denver Broncos]]. Bell won his second Super Bowl when the Chiefs defeated the Eagles 38–35 in [[Super Bowl LVII]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LVII – Philadelphia Eagles vs. Kansas City Chiefs – February 12th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202302120phi.htm |access-date=March 24, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In the 2023 season, Bell won his third Super Bowl championship when the Chiefs defeated the 49ers 25–22 in [[Super Bowl LVIII]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maaddi |first=Rob |date=February 12, 2024 |title=Patrick Mahomes rallies the Chiefs to second straight Super Bowl title, 25–22 over 49ers in overtime |url=https://apnews.com/article/super-bowl-2024-score-chiefs-49ers-49b5dca51c05ab0f259cef0d7da76c2d |access-date=February 14, 2024 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bell is the son of former NFL defensive end [[Mark Bell (defensive end)|Mark Bell]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mark Bell Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BellMa22.htm |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> and nephew of former defensive end [[Mike Bell (defensive lineman)|Mike Bell]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mike Bell Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BellMi20.htm |access-date=February 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Bell is a devout [[Catholicism|Roman Catholic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rohde |first=John |title=Bishop, Bedlam, & Beyond |url=https://static.soonersports.com/custompages/microsites/14fb_bell/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923183552/https://static.soonersports.com/custompages/microsites/14fb_bell/index.html |archive-date=September 23, 2020 |access-date=April 21, 2020 |website=Sooner Sports}}</ref>

'''Bishop Sankey''' (born September 15, 1992) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the second round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. Sankey played [[college football]] for the [[Washington Huskies football|Washington Huskies]].

After starting 12 games over two seasons with the Titans, Sankey then had stints with the [[New England Patriots]], [[Kansas City Chiefs]] and [[Minnesota Vikings]] over the next two seasons without seeing any game action. After a year away from football, Sankey saw game action again playing for the [[San Diego Fleet]] of the short-lived [[Alliance of American Football]] in 2019. Later that year, he was signed to the [[practice roster]] of the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). After the cancellation of the 2020 CFL season, he signed an extension with the Argonauts in 2021, but retired before the season began.

==Early life==
Born in 1992 in [[Wadsworth, Ohio]], to Julie Anne Becker and Christopher Daniel Sankey, Bishop spent his early years with his mother, Julie, and grandparents, William and Carol Becker, in Wadsworth, Ohio until age 7.<ref name="gpsoar">{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Greg |date=September 22, 2010 |title=G-Prep's Sankey on a roll |url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2010/sep/22/g-preps-sankey-roll/ |access-date=May 3, 2014 |website=Spokesman-Review}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bell |first=Gregg |date=August 20, 2014 |title=Unleashed: Inside The Great Unknown, Bishop Sankey |url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209262935&DB_OEM_ID=30200 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140712123049/http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30200&ATCLID=209262935 |archive-date=July 12, 2014 |access-date=August 25, 2014 |website=GoHuskies.com}}</ref> He moved with his father, a [[Non-commissioned officer#United States|non-commissioned officer]] in the [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]] to [[Fairchild Air Force Base|Fairchild AFB]] near [[Spokane, Washington]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-10-09 |title=Untold Stories: Bishop Sankey's unparalleled strength |url=https://www.krem.com/article/sports/high-school/hs-football/untold-stories-bishop-sankeys-unparalleled-strength/293-c69eb30f-3a5c-4109-a5bb-71f58dd117df |access-date=2025-05-23 |website=krem.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-12-12 |title=Last time Washington, Boise State met in Las Vegas, Bishop Sankey ruled |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/dec/12/last-time-washington-boise-state-met-in-las-vegas-/ |access-date=2025-05-23 |website=Spokesman.com |language=en}}</ref> when Sankey was in the eighth grade, relocating from [[Wright-Patterson Air Force Base|Wright-Patterson AFB]] near [[Dayton, Ohio]].<ref name="mbgslhap">{{Cite web |last=Siemon |first=Dean |date=October 2, 2013 |title=Military backgrounds set local Huskies apart |url=http://www.nwguardian.com/2013/10/03/16525/military-backgrounds-set-local.html |access-date=May 3, 2014 |website=Northwest Guardian |agency=Joint Base Lewis-McChord}}</ref> He finished that school year in 2007 at the middle school in [[Cheney, Washington|Cheney]], then enrolled as a freshman at [[Gonzaga Preparatory School|Gonzaga Prep]] in Spokane and graduated in 2011.<ref name=gpsoar/> When he was a sophomore in 2008, the Bullpups compiled an 8–2 record. That season, Sankey [[Rush (gridiron football)|rushed]] for 526 yards while splitting time in the backfield, averaging 10.5 yards per [[Carry (gridiron football)|carry]]. He earned All-Greater Spokane League first-team and All-State Class 4A honorable mention as a junior, amassing 2,011 yards with 17 rushing [[touchdown]]s in nine contests. He opened the season with four 200-yard rushing performances and by midseason, he had shattered the previous school record of 1,299 yards on the ground by [[Tim Lappano]] in 1974. As a senior, Sankey established league and district season and career rushing records. He totaled 2,518 yards with 33 touchdowns on 281 carries (8.96 ypc), becoming the only player in district annals to produce a pair of "top ten" rushing seasons on the annual record chart. That season would see him gain 359 yards against [[Mead High School|Mead]], the third-highest game total in GSL annals. Sankey closed out his career as the state and [[Washington Interscholastic Activities Association#Greater Spokane District Eight|Greater Spokane League]] record-holder with 4,355 yards rushing. His 198 points scored set another season mark and his career total of 306 points rank third. He was named the Inland Northwest amateur athlete of the year for his efforts.<ref name="gslrush">{{Cite web |title=GSL Football All-Time Records: Rushing |url=http://greaterspokaneleague.org/gsl-football-all-time-records |access-date=May 3, 2014 |publisher=Greater Spokane League |archive-date=May 4, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140504070416/http://greaterspokaneleague.org/gsl-football-all-time-records |url-status=dead }}</ref> Following his senior season, Sankey was invited to perform at the U.S. Army National Combine, attended by over 500 players, where he recorded a [[20-yard shuttle]] time of 3.90, the second-best at the event, while his 4.4 clocking in the [[40-yard dash]] was also the best for any player in attendance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The book on: Bishop Sankey |url=http://www.scout.com/nfl/story/1395116-the-book-on-bishop-sankey}}</ref>

Sankey was also a member of the Gonzaga Prep [[track and field]] team, where he performed as a sprinter and as a member of the relay teams, in addition to performing as a jumper. As a sophomore, he recorded season-bests of 11.40 in the [[100 meters]] at the Jesuit Twilight Outdoor Relays,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jesuit Twilight Relays - Track & Field Meet |url=http://www.athletic.net:8081/TrackAndField/meet/61046 |website=Athletic.net}}{{Dead link|date=April 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> along with a 6.43-meter (21'1") [[long jump]] and a 12.48-meter (40'11.25") [[triple jump]] in Greater Spokane League competition.<ref>{{Cite web |title=GSL 4A District Meet - Track & Field Meet |url=http://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/meet/83413 |website=Athletic.net}}</ref> He also ran a leg on the Bullpups' [[4 × 100 metres relay|4x100]], [[4 × 200 metres relay|4x200]] and [[4 × 400 metres relay|4x400 relay]] teams. The following season, Sankey again starred for the school's outdoor track team. He posted a season-best 11.28 seconds in the 100 meters at the GSL District Meet,<ref>{{Cite web |title=GSL Districts Day 2 - Track & Field Meet |url=http://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/meet/88619 |website=Athletic.net}}</ref> and 23.21 in the [[200 meters]] at the regionals,<ref>{{Cite web |title=GSL\CBBN Regionals Day 1 - Track & Field Meet |url=http://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/meet/88620 |website=Athletic.net}}</ref> followed by a [[400 meters|400-meter]] clocking of 54.84.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ferris/Shadle/G-Prep/NWC Jamboree - Track & Field Meet |url=http://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/meet/90274 |website=Athletic.net}}</ref> As a senior, he boasted season-best times of 11.54 in the 100 meters, 23.94 in the 200 and 55.14 in the 400. He also ran a leg on the 4x100 and 4x200 relay teams that placed second in both events at the Ray Cockrum Relays.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ray Cockrum Relays - Track & Field Meet |url=http://www.athletic.net:8081/TrackAndField/meet/112595 |website=Athletic.net}}{{Dead link|date=April 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Regarded as a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Sankey initially gave a "soft verbal" commitment to [[Washington State Cougars football|Washington State University]] as a junior in December 2009,<ref name="gpsoar" /> then changed his mind as a senior - “on [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] day” & accepted a [[Athletic scholarship|scholarship]] from head coach [[Steve Sarkisian]] to play football at the [[Washington Huskies football|University of Washington]].<ref name="n758">{{cite web | last=Vorel | first=Mike | title=Last time Washington, Boise State met in Las Vegas, Bishop Sankey ruled | website=Spokesman.com | date=2019-12-12 | url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/dec/12/last-time-washington-boise-state-met-in-las-vegas-/ | access-date=2025-01-06}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Bishop Sankey 2013.jpg|thumb|left|Sankey with Washington in 2013]]
Sankey appeared in 38 games for the [[Washington Huskies football|Washington Huskies]], starting his last 25 contests. He carried the ball 644 times for 3,496 yards (third-most in Huskies' history) and scored 37 touchdowns on the ground, while also adding 567 yards and one more score on 67 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] (8.46 ypc) and 134 yards on seven [[kickoff return]]s (19.14 avg) for a total of 4,197 [[all-purpose yards]] (110.45 ypg). In 2013, with a 200-yard game against Washington State in the [[Apple Cup]], he finished the game and the regular season with 1,775 yards for the season, breaking [[Corey Dillon]]'s 1996 record of 1,695 yards. On the same play on which he passed Dillon, a seven-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, he also broke [[Napoleon Kaufman]]'s school career rushing touchdowns record, with his 35th. He decided to forego his senior season and enter the [[NFL draft]] in January 2013.

===Freshman season===
{{see also|2011 Washington Huskies football team}}
After rushing for 2,518 yards as a senior in high school, Sankey only carried the ball 28 times as a [[true freshman]] at Washington in [[2011 Washington Huskies football team|2011]], but made the most of his limited chances as he gained 187 yards, an average of 6.68 yards per attempt. He scored just once, but had big carries that set up eight touchdown drives and key receptions that resulted in two more scoring marches for the Huskies. Nine of Sankey's carries resulted in first downs, with eight of those gaining at least 10 yards. He also added six receptions and in the Alamo Bowl's wild 67–56 loss to [[2011 Baylor Bears football team|Baylor]], and also handled kickoff return duties.

===Sophomore season===
{{see also|2012 Washington Huskies football team}}
With [[Chris Polk]] having left for the National Football League, the Huskies opened the 2012 campaign with Sankey in a reserve role. When junior [[Halfback (American football)|halfback]] Jesse Callier was injured in Washington's first game against [[2012 San Diego State Aztecs football team|San Diego State]], Sankey stepped into the starting lineup the next week and never relinquished his role with the first unit. He was the MVP of the [[2012 Maaco Bowl Las Vegas]] after rushing for 205 yards and 74 receiving yards on six receptions.<ref>{{Cite news |date=December 23, 2012 |title=Maaco Bowl notebook: UW's Sankey earns MVP honors in loss |work=Idaho Press-Tribune |url=http://www.idahopress.com/sports/boise/bsf-football/maaco-bowl-notebook-uw-s-sankey-earns-mvp-honors-in/article_d2118120-4ce0-11e2-8cb2-001a4bcf887a.html |access-date=May 3, 2014}}</ref> Sankey ended up rushing for 1,439 yards on 289 carries (4.98 ypc), both rank third on the school season-record chart. His 16 touchdown runs are surpassed by only [[Corey Dillon]] (who had 24 touchdowns in 1996) on the Huskies annual record list.<ref name="uwhsshn">{{Cite news |last=Jude |first=Adam |date=August 10, 2013 |title=Bishop Sankey, UW's humble star, shines on field and in the classroom |work=Seattle Times |url=http://seattletimes.com/html/huskyfootball/2021586648_huskyfootball11xml.html |access-date=May 3, 2014}}</ref> Sankey averaged 110.69 yards per game on the ground, the 19th-best average in the [[NCAA Football Bowl Subdivision]] ranks that year. He also served as a safety valve for quarterback [[Keith Price]], catching 16 of the 22 passes targeted to him, good for 249 yards. He led the team in scoring with 96 points and registered 1,688 all-purpose yards, the seventh-best figure by a Husky in a season.<ref name="diall">{{Cite news |last=Brewer |first=Jerry |date=November 29, 2013 |title=Huskies' Bishop Sankey does it all – except brag |work=Seattle Times |url=http://seattletimes.com/html/jerrybrewer/2022364832_brewer30xml.html |url-status=dead |access-date=May 3, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140126055802/http://seattletimes.com/html/jerrybrewer/2022364832_brewer30xml.html |archive-date=January 26, 2014}}</ref>

===Junior season===
{{see also|2013 Washington Huskies football team}}
After being named one of the team's offensive [[team captain|captains]], Sankey rewarded his teammates for that honor when he exploded for 161 yards and two touchdowns on 25 carries in the 2013 season opener against [[2013 Boise State Broncos football team|Boise State]]. He also came up with other big carries that set up two more touchdown drives, along with a big reception that led to a [[field goal]]. With his mother, aunts and uncles in the stands at Chicago's [[Soldier Field]], Sankey exploded for a career-best 208 yards and a touchdown on a career-high 35 carries against [[2013 Illinois Fighting Illini football team|Illinois]]. He would establish school career and season records when he again reached the 200-yard rushing level in the [[Apple Cup|2013 Apple Cup]] against [[2013 Washington State Cougars football team|Washington State]]. During his junior season, Sankey also proved to be a highly capable blocker, registering seventy-six knockdowns and 10 touchdown-resulting blocks.
<ref name="diall" /> He was named Second-team [[2013 College Football All-America Team|All-American]] and First-team All-[[2013 All-Pac-12 Conference football team]] at the end of the season.

Sankey entered the [[2014 NFL draft]] after his junior season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fornelli |first=Tom |date=December 30, 2013 |title=Washington RB Bishop Sankey to enter NFL Draft |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/eye-on-college-football/24392399/washington-rb-bishop-sankey-to-enter-nfl-draft |access-date=May 3, 2014 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref> He finished his college career as Washington's career leader in rushing touchdowns and third all-time in rushing yards.<ref name=CFLextension>{{Cite news|date=December 28, 2020|title=Bladek extension among 11 Argos transactions|work=CFL.ca|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2020/12/28/bladek-extension-among-11-argos-transactions/|access-date=December 29, 2020}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
The [[Tennessee Titans]] selected Sankey in the second round of the 2014 NFL draft.<ref name="frsel">{{Cite news |last=Jude |first=Adam |date=May 9, 2014 |title=UW's Bishop Sankey becomes first running back drafted, heads to Tennessee Titans |work=Seattle Times |agency=Husky football blog |url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/huskyfootball/2014/05/09/uws-bishop-sankey-first-running-back-drafted/ |access-date=May 10, 2014}}</ref><ref name="uwptpl">{{Cite news |last=Jude |first=Adam |date=May 9, 2014 |title=UW's Bishop Sankey 'pumped' to play for the Tennessee Titans |work=Seattle Times |agency=Husky football blog |url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/huskyfootball/2014/05/09/uws-bishop-sankey-pumped-to-play-for-the-tennessee-titans/ |access-date=May 10, 2014}}</ref> Chosen with the 54th overall pick, he was the first [[running back]] off the board, the latest for a first running back in the history of the [[National Football League draft|NFL draft]].<ref name="sktted">{{Cite news |last=Reyes |first=Lorenzo |date=May 10, 2014 |title=Bishop Sankey, Titans end NFL draft's historic RB drought |work=USA Today |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/draft/2014/05/09/bishop-sankey-tennessee-titans-running-backs-nfl-draft/8923543/ |access-date=May 10, 2014}}</ref><ref name="pkbtt">{{Cite news |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=May 9, 2014 |title=Bishop Sankey picked by Titans in second round |work=The Tennessean |url=http://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/nfl/titans/2014/05/09/bishop-sankey-titans-second-round/8923405/ |access-date=May 10, 2014}}</ref>

On June 17, 2014, Sankey signed a four-year contract with the Titans. Sankey scored his first NFL touchdown against the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on September 28. Sankey finished his rookie season with 569 yards on 152 carries and two touchdowns. Sankey recorded an additional 133 receiving yards on 18 receptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bishop Sankey |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/gamelog/_/id/16794/year/2014/bishop-sankey |access-date=April 12, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Sankey opened the 2015 season with a career-high 74 yards on 12 carries and one touchdown. However following Week 6, Sankey would only receive eight carries for 34 yards and six receptions and was a healthy scratch three times.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bishop Sankey |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/gamelog/_/id/16794/bishop-sankey |access-date=April 12, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Sankey started only three games in 2015, down from the previous year's nine.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bishop Sankey 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SankBi00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On September 2, 2016, Sankey was released by the Titans as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=September 2, 2016 |title=Titans Down to 53 Players: A Position-by-Position Look |url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Down-to-53-Players-A-Position-by-Position-Look/628127bc-7013-4906-a04d-bd1f9e8ce8fa |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170807023144/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Down-to-53-Players-A-Position-by-Position-Look/628127bc-7013-4906-a04d-bd1f9e8ce8fa |archive-date=August 7, 2017}}</ref> Sankey started 12 of the 29 games he played for the Titans, totaling 199 rushes, 762 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. He also added 32 receptions on 45 targets for 272 yards (8.5 yards per catch) and a score through the air from 2014 to 2015.

===New England Patriots===
On September 5, 2016, Sankey was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2016 |title=Patriots sign eight players to the practice squad |url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2016/09/05/patriots-sign-eight-players-practice-squad |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170916232339/http://www.patriots.com/news/2016/09/05/patriots-sign-eight-players-practice-squad |archive-date=September 16, 2017 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On November 1, 2016, Sankey was signed by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] off the Patriots' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thorman |first=Joel |date=November 1, 2016 |title=Chiefs sign RB Bishop Sankey |url=http://www.arrowheadpride.com/2016/11/1/13487156/chiefs-sign-rb-bishop-sankey-off-patriots-practice-squad |access-date=November 1, 2016 |website=Arrowhead Pride}}</ref> He was released by the Chiefs on November 22.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 22, 2016 |title=Chiefs Waive RB Bishop Sankey |url=http://nfltraderumors.co/chiefs-waive-rb-bishop-sankey/}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
On November 25, 2016, Sankey was signed to the [[Minnesota Vikings]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ratke |first=Kyle |date=November 25, 2016 |title=Vikings sign RB Bishop Sankey to practice squad |url=http://vikingswire.usatoday.com/2016/11/25/vikings-sign-rb-bishop-sankey-to-practice-squad/ |website=VikingsWire}}</ref> He signed a reserve/futures contract with the Vikings on January 2, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Craig |date=January 2, 2017 |title=Vikings Sign 9 Practice Squad Players to Futures Contracts |url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Sign-9-Practice-Squad-Players-to-Futures-Contracts/fa006209-f66e-44c0-b86d-466fa410adb1 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906225207/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Sign-9-Practice-Squad-Players-to-Futures-Contracts/fa006209-f66e-44c0-b86d-466fa410adb1 |archive-date=September 6, 2017 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

===San Diego Fleet===
On September 5, 2018, Sankey signed with [[San Diego Fleet]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]] (AAF) for the 2019 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nguyen |first=Alexander |date=September 5, 2018 |title=San Diego AAF Team Signs Former Washington Quarterback |url=https://timesofsandiego.com/sports/2018/09/05/san-diego-aaf-team-signs-former-washington-quarterback/ |access-date=September 14, 2018 |website=timesofsandiego.com}}</ref> He suffered an injury before the season began and was placed on the roster exempt list,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldberg |first=Jeff |date=January 30, 2019 |title='It's Go time': Roster in place, Fleet excited for season debut |url=https://aaf.com/its-go-time-roster-in-place-fleet-excited-for-season-debut |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202041613/https://aaf.com/its-go-time-roster-in-place-fleet-excited-for-season-debut |archive-date=February 2, 2019 |access-date=February 1, 2019 |publisher=[[Alliance of American Football]]}}</ref> a designation that later became [[injured reserve]]. He was promoted to the active roster on March 4.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gartin |first=Zachary |date=March 4, 2019 |title=San Diego Fleet Make a Flurry of Roster Moves in Response to Injuries |url=https://eastvillagetimes.com/2019/03/san-diego-fleet-make-a-flurry-of-roster-moves-in-response-to-injuries/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306044734/https://eastvillagetimes.com/2019/03/san-diego-fleet-make-a-flurry-of-roster-moves-in-response-to-injuries/ |archive-date=March 6, 2019 |access-date=March 4, 2019 |publisher=East Village Times}}</ref> In the remaining 4 games prior to the AAF's bankruptcy, Sankey recorded 119 yards on 30 rushing attempts, as well as 5 receptions for 20 yards.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://noextrapoints.com/players/bishop-sankey/|title=Bishop Sankey}}</ref> The league ceased operations in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

===Toronto Argonauts===
With two weeks remaining in the [[2019 CFL season]], Sankey was signed to the practice roster by the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).<ref>{{Cite web|last=Zicarelli|first=Frank|date=October 24, 2019|url=https://montrealgazette.com/sports/football/cfl/toronto-argonauts/argos-acquire-a-bishop-as-chess-game-for-2020-adds-a-new-piece/wcm/3eb5d4c0-3618-49c4-b0ff-a07911733654|title=Argos acquire a Bishop as chess game for 2020 adds a new piece|work=Montreal Gazette|access-date=February 1, 2022}}</ref> The CFL cancelled its [[2020 CFL season|2020 season]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. He signed a contract extension with the Argonauts on December 28, 2020.<ref name=CFLextension/> He retired from football on July 10, 2021, on the first day of the Argos' [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Boclair|first=David|date=July 11, 2021|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/titans/news/tennessee-titans-nfl-toronto-argonauts-cfl-bishop-sankey-retires|title=Former Titans Running Back Calls it a Career|work=Sports Illustrated|access-date=February 1, 2022}}</ref>

'''Robby Blake Bortles''' (born April 28, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for eight seasons, primarily with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[UCF Knights football|UCF Knights]], winning [[American Athletic Conference football individual awards#Offensive Player of the Year|AAC Offensive Player of the Year]] in 2013. Bortles was selected by the Jaguars third overall in the [[2014 NFL draft]].

As the Jaguars' starting quarterback from 2014 to 2018, Bortles set franchise records for single-season passing yards and touchdowns in 2015. His most successful season was in 2017 when he helped bring the Jaguars to their first division title and [[AFC Championship Game]] appearance since 1999. However, Bortles also led the league in interceptions in 2015 and had a league-high 75 interceptions by the end of his five years with Jacksonville. After being released by the Jaguars in 2018, he spent his final three seasons as a backup for the [[Los Angeles Rams]], [[Denver Broncos]], [[Green Bay Packers]], and [[New Orleans Saints]].

==Early life==
Robby Blake Bortles<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Lion's Tale – Volume 50, Issue 7 |url=https://issuu.com/thelionstale/docs/edition7final/12 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201005193704/https://issuu.com/thelionstale/docs/edition7final/12 |archive-date=October 5, 2020 |access-date=August 27, 2016 |website=iSSUU.com |date=May 20, 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Says |first=Shae |date=September 1, 2015 |title=Blake Bortles sure 'taint' trying to impress anyone |url=http://www.thespecktator.com/2015/09/01/blake-bortles-sure-taint-trying-impress-anyone/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160921001633/http://www.thespecktator.com/2015/09/01/blake-bortles-sure-taint-trying-impress-anyone/ |archive-date=September 21, 2016 |access-date=August 27, 2016 |website=Specktator}}</ref> attended [[Oviedo High School]] in [[Oviedo, Florida]], where he excelled in [[high school football|football]] and [[baseball]] for the Lions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crawford |first=Heather |date=January 18, 2018 |title=Blake Bortles' high school coach tells all about the quarterback |url=http://www.firstcoastnews.com/article/sports/nfl/jacksonville-jaguars/blake-bortles-high-school-coach-tells-all-about-the-quarterback/77-509313653 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201005193705/https://www.firstcoastnews.com/article/sports/nfl/jacksonville-jaguars/blake-bortles-high-school-coach-tells-all-about-the-quarterback/77-509313653 |archive-date=October 5, 2020 |access-date=March 13, 2018 |publisher=WTLV |language=en-US}}</ref> As a senior, he completed 151 of 233 passes for 2,211 yards with 27 [[touchdown]]s and seven [[interception]]s. He finished his high school career with a [[Seminole County, Florida|Seminole County]] record 5,576 career passing yards and 53 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Denton |first=John |date=October 17, 2011 |title=QB Blake Bortles Helps When Asked |url=https://today.ucf.edu/qb-blake-bortles-helps-when-asked/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171109023341/https://today.ucf.edu/qb-blake-bortles-helps-when-asked/ |archive-date=November 9, 2017 |access-date=November 8, 2017 |website=UCF News – University of Central Florida Articles – Orlando, FL News |language=en-US}}</ref>

Labeled a three-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Bortles was listed as the No. 44 pro-style [[quarterback]] in his class.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rivals.com pro-style quarterbacks 2010 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-2388 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140225194409/https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-2388 |archive-date=February 25, 2014 |access-date=May 10, 2014 |website=[[Rivals.com]]}}</ref> Bortles chose UCF over offers from [[Colorado State Rams football|Colorado State]], [[Purdue Boilermakers football|Purdue]], [[Tulane Green Wave football|Tulane]], and [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football|Western Kentucky]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ryzewski |first=Steven |date=May 8, 2014 |title=The Bortles File: Covering Blake Bortles through the years |url=http://www.seminolechronicle.com/vnews/display.v/ART/2014/05/08/536b812d729ce |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140510182246/http://www.seminolechronicle.com/vnews/display.v/ART/2014/05/08/536b812d729ce |archive-date=May 10, 2014 |access-date=May 10, 2014 |website=[[Seminole Chronicle]]}}"After turning down offers from Purdue, Colorado State and Tulane, Oviedo quarterback Blake Bortles committed to UCF on Saturday."</ref>

==College career==
Bortles accepted the offer from UCF, which was the first college to offer him a scholarship and was located near his home. He was [[redshirted]] as a [[true freshman]] in 2010. As a redshirt freshman in 2011, he played in 10 games, completing 75 of 110 passes for 958 yards with six touchdowns and three interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Bortles 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/blake-bortles-1/gamelog/2011/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201005193707/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/blake-bortles-1/gamelog/2011/ |archive-date=October 5, 2020 |access-date=December 31, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> As a sophomore in 2012, he started all 14 games at quarterback. He completed 251 of 399 passes for 3,059 yards with 25 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He also rushed for 285 yards and scored eight touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Bortles 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/blake-bortles-1/gamelog/2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201005193722/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/blake-bortles-1/gamelog/2012 |archive-date=October 5, 2020 |access-date=December 31, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tenorio |first=Paul |date=August 27, 2013 |title=New year brings new expectations for UCF quarterback Blake Bortles |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2013/08/27/new-year-brings-new-expectations-for-ucf-quarterback-blake-bortles/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117031616/http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/2013-08-27/sports/os-ucf-akron-football-0828-20130827_1_blake-bortles-jeff-godfrey-ucf-coach-george-o-leary |archive-date=November 17, 2015 |access-date=May 10, 2014 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]}}</ref>
He was the MVP of the [[2012 Beef 'O' Brady's Bowl]] after completing 22 of 32 passes for 271 yards with three touchdowns and 79 rushing yards against the [[2012 Ball State Cardinals football team|Ball State Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tenorio |first=Paul |date=December 21, 2012 |title=UCF's Blake Bortles leads Knights to 38–17 win over Ball State in bowl |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2012/12/21/ucfs-blake-bortles-leads-knights-to-38-17-win-over-ball-state-in-bowl/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222100634/http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/2012-12-21/sports/os-live-updates-ucf-ball-state-beef-bowl_1_latavius-murray-ucf-coach-george-o-leary-ucf-quarterback |archive-date=December 22, 2015 |access-date=May 10, 2014 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]}}</ref>

[[File:BlakeBortesUCF2013.JPG|thumb|Bortles with UCF in 2013]]
In 2013, Bortles led the Knights to the inaugural championship of the [[American Athletic Conference]], earning the league's [[Automatic Qualifying conference|automatic berth]] to a [[Bowl Championship Series|BCS]] [[Bowl game|bowl]], the [[2014 Fiesta Bowl (January)|Tostitos Fiesta Bowl]]. Passing for 301 yards and rushing for 93 yards and four touchdowns, Bortles led UCF to an upset of fifth-ranked [[2013 Baylor Bears football team|Baylor]], 52–42. Bortles was named the Offensive MVP of the game, which was UCF's first major bowl win in school history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gillespie |first=Ryan |date=January 2, 2014 |title=No. 15 UCF stuns No. 5 Baylor in Fiesta Bowl |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/bowls/2014/01/02/central-florida-ucf-knights-baylor-bears-fiesta-bowl-blake-bortles/4284975/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201005193722/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/bowls/2014/01/02/central-florida-ucf-knights-baylor-bears-fiesta-bowl-blake-bortles/4284975/ |archive-date=October 5, 2020 |access-date=May 10, 2014 |website=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> In his final collegiate season, he was 259-of-382 for 3,581 yards, 25 touchdowns, and nine interceptions. He added 87 rushes for 272 yards and six rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Bortles 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/blake-bortles-1/gamelog/2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180101030520/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/blake-bortles-1/gamelog/2013 |archive-date=January 1, 2018 |access-date=December 31, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

As a starter from the 2012 and 2013 seasons, Bortles had a 22–5 ({{Winning percentage|22|5}}) record for the Knights. As of 2016, his career passer rating of 153.9 is the highest for any UCF quarterback with at least 500 pass attempts and he was fourth in career completions, yards, and touchdowns behind [[Daunte Culpepper]], Ryan Schneider, and [[Darin Hinshaw]].<ref>{{Cite web |year=2016 |title=2016 UCF Football Yearbook |url=https://issuu.com/ucf_athletics/docs/2016_ucf_football_media_guide |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201005193737/https://issuu.com/ucf_athletics/docs/2016_ucf_football_media_guide |archive-date=October 5, 2020 |access-date=September 27, 2017 |website=issuu |pages=122–125 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=UCF Knights Passing |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/central-florida/passing.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313095247/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/central-florida/passing.html |archive-date=March 13, 2018 |access-date=March 13, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>
