'''Billy Joe Owens Jr.''' (born December 2, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He also played in the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) for the [[Orlando Predators]], [[Charlotte Rage]], [[Connecticut Coyotes]] and [[Portland Forest Dragons]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]].

==Early life==
Owens attended [[Christian Brothers Academy (DeWitt, New York)|Christian Brothers High School]], where he played as a [[running back]], [[wide receiver]] and [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]]. He received All-state honors as a senior. He also lettered in [[basketball]], [[baseball]] and [[track and field|track]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Holbreich |first=Curt |date=October 28, 1986 |title=Syracuse Home For Pitt's Owens |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1144&dat=19861028&id=5rsqAAAAIBAJ&sjid=BmMEAAAAIBAJ&pg=5250,7605791&hl=es |access-date=September 24, 2018 |website=The Pittsburgh Press|via=Google News}}</ref>

He accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Pittsburgh]], where he was switched between [[running back]] to [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] as a freshman, but still managed to average 8.3 yards per carry (14 carries for 116 yards and one [[touchdown]]). In 1984, he was [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] after being lost for the season with a knee injury.

As a sophomore, he became the starter at [[free safety]] toward the end of the season, although he was used as a backup [[running back]] in some games.<ref>{{cite web| url=
https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1129&dat=19851023&id=87NRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=QG4DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6800,6084908&hl=es | title=Double Duty Pitt's Owens Ready To Play Both Ways Against Middies | accessdate=September 24, 2018}}</ref> He was a part of a secondary that was called "The Burnt Toast Patrol", after giving up a school record 2,283 passing yards.<ref>{{cite web| url=
https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1129&dat=19870415&id=Aa9RAAAAIBAJ&sjid=5m0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6895,5076686&hl=es  | title=Pitt Secondary Now The Upper Crust | accessdate=September 24, 2018}}</ref>

As a junior, he was moved to [[strong safety]] and was fourth on the team with 106 tackles. He also tied with [[Quintin Jones (American football)|Quintin Jones]] for the club lead with 4 interceptions. He had a career-high 16 tackles against [[North Carolina State University]].

As a senior, he tallied 88 tackles (fifth on the team), 2 sacks, 2 fumble recoveries and one interception. He also averaged 22.4 yards as a part-time kick off returner. Against [[West Virginia University]], he tallied 9 tackles, one sack and 2 forced fumbles, including the one that set up the winning field goal in Pittsburgh's 6-3 win. He made a season-high 10 tackles in the upset 30–22 win against the [[University of Notre Dame]]. He had a memorable play against [[Penn State University]], when he returned an interception 69 yards to seal a 10-0 victory with 42 seconds remaining in the game. It was Pitt's first shutout over Penn State since 1955 (a 20-0 victory).<ref>{{cite web| url=http://articles.philly.com/1987-11-15/sports/26171597_1_penn-state-pitt-pitt-stadium-pitt-coach-mike-gottfried | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160927121409/http://articles.philly.com/1987-11-15/sports/26171597_1_penn-state-pitt-pitt-stadium-pitt-coach-mike-gottfried | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 27, 2016 | title=Penn State Is Subdued By Pitt, 10-0 | accessdate=September 24, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1129&dat=19871116&id=YM5RAAAAIBAJ&sjid=620DAAAAIBAJ&pg=5099,4972276&hl=es | title=Panthers Fitted For Bluebonnet | accessdate=September 24, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Dallas Cowboys===
Owens was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the tenth round (263rd overall) of the [[1988 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1988 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1988/draft.htm |access-date=2023-09-23 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He made the team as a backup [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] and played on passing downs as a [[linebacker]]. He posed 13 [[special teams]] tackles (fourth on the team), 7 defensive tackles, 2 passes defensed and one sack. He was waived on September 5, [[1989 NFL season|1989]].

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On March 19, [[1990 NFL season|1990]], he was signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2002&dat=19900320&id=X7ciAAAAIBAJ&sjid=JrUFAAAAIBAJ&pg=1009,3908676&hl=es |title=Steelers Sign Billy Owens | accessdate=September 24, 2018}}</ref> He was released on September 3.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1298&dat=19900904&id=H7FYAAAAIBAJ&sjid=NosDAAAAIBAJ&pg=903,5553957&hl=es |title=Monday's NFL Transactions | accessdate=September 24, 2018}}</ref>

===Orlando Thunder===
In [[1991 WLAF season|1991]], he signed with the [[Orlando Thunder]] of the [[World League of American Football]]. He registered 49 tackles (second on the team), 11 [[special teams]] tackles (led the team), one interception, 4 forced fumbles and one fumble recovery. He was released on March 10, 1992.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=860&dat=19920311&id=jm9UAAAAIBAJ&sjid=Uo8DAAAAIBAJ&pg=5338,962169&hl=es |title=Transactions | accessdate=September 24, 2018}}</ref>

===Montreal Machine===
On May 5, [[1992 WLAF season|1992]], he was claimed off waivers by the [[Montreal Machine]] of the [[World League of American Football]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=861&dat=19920506&id=CRtIAAAAIBAJ&sjid=HoEMAAAAIBAJ&pg=1123,5346622&hl=es |title=Transactions | accessdate=September 24, 2018}}</ref>

===Orlando Predators===
In [[1993 Arena Football League season|1993]], he signed with the [[Orlando Predators]] of the [[Arena Football League]]. He was declared inactive for the first four weeks. In [[1994 AFL season|1994]], he registered 46 receptions, 16 touchdowns, 47 tackles and 4 interceptions, however he asked for guarantees if the Predators did well in the playoffs, and the team reacted by suspending him before the semifinals game against the [[Massachusetts Marauders]] (a 51-42 win).

===Charlotte Rage===
On May 17, [[1996 Arena Football League season|1996]], he was traded along with Reggie Robinson to the [[Connecticut Coyotes]] in exchange for [[Les Barley]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.courant.com/news/connecticut/hc-xpm-1996-05-18-9605180430-story.html |title=Coyotes' Gaston Tackles His Critics | accessdate=September 24, 2018}}</ref> He played in 3 games.

===Portland Forest Dragons===
In [[1997 Arena Football League season|1997]], he signed with [[Portland Forest Dragons]]. He was released on March 21, [[1998 Arena Football League season|1998]].

==Personal life==
Owens grew up three blocks from the [[Syracuse University]] campus and was a [[ball boy]] for the Syracuse basketball team from 1977 to 1980.{{fact|date=June 2025}}

'''Blair Brown''' (born May 27, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio Bobcats football|Ohio Bobcats]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gillis |first=Andew |date=April 19, 2017 |title=Football: Meet Blair Brown, one of the NFL draft's most underrated prospects |url=http://www.thepostathens.com/article/2017/04/ohio-football-nfl-draft-blair-brown |access-date=November 23, 2024 |website=ThePostAthens.com}}</ref>

==College career==
Brown was ranked first in [[Football Bowl Subdivision]] (FBS) in [[tackled gridiron|tackling]] efficiency with just three misses and 96 solo tackles while at [[Ohio University]].<ref name="PFF.com">{{Cite web |last=PFF.com |date=April 1, 2017 |title=PFF Scouting Report:Blair Brown, LB, Ohio |url=https://www.pff.com/news/draft-pff-scouting-report-blair-brown-lb-ohio |access-date=March 4, 2020 |website=PFF.com}}</ref> In 2016, only [[Reuben Foster]] had higher overall and run-defense grades according to [[Pro Football Focus]] than Brown's 92.4 and 91.5. Brown's 131 total tackles tied for the second-most among FBS [[inside linebackers]]. Brown was ranked third in FBS in run-stop percentage and had 47 stops.<ref name="PFF.com" />

==Professional career==
===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Brown was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the fifth round, 148th overall, in the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser, John |date=April 29, 2017 |title=No. 148: Jaguars select LB Blair Brown |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/No-148-Jaguars-select-LB-Blair-Brown/621052f8-ac99-4aef-94b1-3b299373324b |access-date=March 4, 2020 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He played in 28 games for the team before he was released on May 9, 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Alper, Josh |date=May 9, 2019 |title=Jaguars release Blair Brown, Donald Payne |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/05/09/jaguars-release-blair-brown-donald-payne/ |access-date=October 19, 2020 |work=NBCSports.com}}</ref>

Brown was charged with domestic battery on May 30, 2019,<ref>{{Cite news |last=DiRocco, Michael |date=May 30, 2019 |title=Ex-Jags LB Brown charged with domestic battery |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26857965/ex-jags-lb-brown-charged-domestic-battery |access-date=October 19, 2020 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> but had the charges dismissed in July 2020 and the NFL announced in October 2020 he would not receive league discipline for the incident.<ref name="Texans">{{Cite news |last=Wilson, Aaron |date=October 17, 2020 |title=Texans working out Blair Brown, Eli Mencer |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/texans/article/Texans-working-out-Blair-Brown-Eli-Mencer-15655970.php |access-date=October 19, 2020 |work=HoustonChronicle.com}}</ref> He worked out for the [[Houston Texans]] on October 17, 2020.<ref name="Texans" />

===Pittsburgh Maulers===
Brown was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Maulers (2022)|Pittsburgh Maulers]] of the [[United States Football League (2022)|United States Football League]] (USFL) in the 31st round of the [[2022 USFL draft]] on February 24, 2022.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1496967472880267264 |user=USFLMaulers |title=Compensatory Pick: The Pittsburgh Maulers selected OLB Blair Brown with the 9th Pick in the 31st Round of the #USFLDraft |date=February 24, 2022 |access-date=April 16, 2022}}</ref> He was transferred to the team's [[practice squad]] before the start of the regular season on April 16.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1515222834326515720 |user=USFLMaulers |title=Roster Updates: Transferred to practice squad: |date=April 16, 2022 |access-date=April 16, 2022}}</ref> He remained on the inactive roster on April 22.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1517405949127905282 |user=USFLMaulers |title=Transferred to inactive roster |date=April 22, 2022 |access-date=April 23, 2022}}</ref> He was transferred to the active roster on April 30.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1520315391280439301 |user=USFLMaulers |title=Roster Updates |date=April 30, 2022 |access-date=April 30, 2022}}</ref> He was released on May 5.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1522126475427676160 |user=USFLMaulers |title=Roster Updates |date=May 5, 2022 |access-date=May 5, 2022}}</ref>

'''William Price''' (born October 11, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for six seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[New York Giants]] and [[Arizona Cardinals]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]], earning [[unanimous All-American]] honors in 2017. He was selected by the Bengals in the first round of the [[2018 NFL draft]].

== Early life ==
Price attended [[Austintown Fitch High School]] in [[Austintown, Ohio]], where he played [[defensive lineman|defensive line]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Billy Price (C): Bio, News, Stats & more|url=https://www.bengals.com/team/players-roster/billy-price/|access-date=2021-09-01|website=www.bengals.com|language=en-US|archive-date=August 2, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180802102034/https://www.bengals.com/team/players-roster/billy-price/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012, as a senior, Price earned First-team All-State and Division I Co-Defensive Player of the Year in Ohio (AP).<ref name=":0" /> In his sophomore and senior seasons, Price helped his Fitch team earn playoff berths.<ref name=":0" />

In high school, Price also competed in the discus and shotput on Fitch's track and field team.<ref name=":0" />

==College career==
A 4-star recruit, Price committed to [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State]] over offers from [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]], [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]], [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]], [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]], and [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]], among others.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Billy-Price-11720/|title = Billy Price, Cincinnati Bengals, Offensive Line}}</ref> In 2013, Price redshirted his freshman season before going on to start all 55 games from 2014 to 2017, breaking the previous OSU school records for starts and consecutive starts of 50.<ref name=":0" />

As a redshirt freshman starting at guard, Price helped Ohio State to the national championship.<ref name=":0" />

Price played his first three seasons at offensive guard before moving to center for his senior season.<ref name=":0" />

As a senior with the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]] in 2017, Price won the [[Rimington Trophy]] as the best collegiate center, earned First-team All-Big Ten honors, and was also named a [[unanimous All-American]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/osu/2017/12/ohio_states_billy_price_wins_r.html|title=Ohio State's Billy Price wins Rimington Trophy for nation's best center: Buckeyes football news|author=Landis, Bill|publisher=Cleveland.com|date=December 7, 2017|access-date=April 10, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dispatch.com/sports/20171207/ohio-state-football--billy-price-named-nations-top-center|title=Ohio State football - Billy Price named nation's top center|first=Tim|last=May|publisher=The Columbus Dispatch|date=December 7, 2017|access-date=April 10, 2018}}</ref>

In 2016 and 2017, Price was elected team captain.<ref name=":0" />

===Cincinnati Bengals===
[[File:Billy Price (50677808006) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Price with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in 2020]]
Price was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] with the 21st overall pick in the first round of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cincinnati Bengals select Ohio State center Billy Price in Round 1|url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2018/4/26/17281650/2018-nfl-draft-results-cincinnati-bengals-ohio-state-billy-price-round-1|website=CincyJungle.com|date=April 26, 2018|access-date=May 26, 2018}}</ref> The Bengals acquired the pick from the [[Buffalo Bills]] along with [[Cordy Glenn]] in an offseason trade.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2018/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He started the first two games at center before missing the next six games with a foot injury. He returned in Week 10 and remained the starter the rest of the season. He was named to the PFWA All-Rookie Team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2018.htm |access-date=2024-07-28 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On April 28, 2021, the Bengals declined the option on Price's contract, making him a free agent in 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals decline fifth-year option for Billy Price, per report|url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2021/4/28/22407793/bengals-fifth-year-option-billy-price-nfl-news|work=Cincy Jungle|publisher=SB Nation|date=April 28, 2021}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On August 30, 2021, Price was traded to the [[New York Giants]] in exchange for defensive tackle [[B. J. Hill (American football)|B. J. Hill]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/price-for-trade-as-bengals-pick-up-d-tackle-from-giants|title=Price For Trade As Bengals Pick Up D-Tackle From Giants|date=August 30, 2021|accessdate=August 30, 2021|first=Geoff|last=Hobson|work=Bengals.com}}</ref> Price started in 15 games in 2021 allowing 24 quarterback pressures and two sacks. Those 24 pressures were the fourth most by a Giants offensive lineman.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants 2022 UFA Primer: OL Billy Price |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/giants/.amp/big-blue-plus/giants-2022-ufa-primer-ol-billy-price|author=Lebitsch, Stephen|website=Si.com|date=February 13, 2022}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On September 14, 2022, Price signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-wr-keelan-cole-to-active-roster-place-wr-dj-turner-reserve-injured | title=Raiders sign WR Keelan Cole to active roster, place WR DJ Turner on reserve/Injured list }}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On October 4, 2022, the [[Arizona Cardinals]] signed Price off the Raiders practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=October 4, 2022 |title=Cardinals Release Andy Isabella; Sign Center Billy Price |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-move-on-from-andy-isabella-sign-center-billy-price |access-date=2022-10-04 |website=www.azcardinals.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Price was named the starting center for Week 7 after [[Rodney Hudson]] injured his knee.<ref>{{cite web|title=The (Billy) Price Is Finally Right, And Friday Before The Vikings|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/the-billy-price-is-finally-right-and-friday-before-the-vikings|author=Urban, Darren|website=azcardinals.com|date=October 28, 2022}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On June 15, 2023, Price signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=2023-06-15 |title=Saints sign Billy Price |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/saints-sign-billy-price |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> He was released by the team on July 20.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-roster-moves-announced-072023|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=July 20, 2023}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On September 27, 2023, Price was signed to the [[Dallas Cowboys]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=September 27, 2023 |title=Cowboys sign Billy Price to practice squad |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/cowboys-sign-billy-price-to-practice-squad |access-date=29 September 2023 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>  His contract expired when the team's season ended January 14, 2024.

=== Retirement ===

On May 25, 2024, Price announced his retirement, citing recovery from a non-sports-related [[pulmonary embolism]] he suffered about a month earlier.<ref>{{cite web |author=Krispinsky, Chad |date=May 25, 2024 |title=Valley Native retires from the NFL after health scare |url=https://www.wkbn.com/sports/valley-native-retires-from-the-nfl-after-health-scare/ |website=wkbn.com}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
At Ohio State, Price majored in Business Administration with a specialization in Operations Management.<ref name=":0" /> In college, Price earned Academic All-Big Ten Conference honors (2014 and 2017) and OSU Scholar-Athlete honors (2013 and 2014) twice each.<ref name=":0" />

'''Billy Pritchett''' (February 22, 1951 –  March 5, 2021) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]]. He played for the [[Cleveland Browns]] in 1975 and for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] from 1976 to 1977.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PritBi00.htm |title=Billy Pritchett Stats |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com |date= |access-date=2019-01-08}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/billypritchett/2523550/profile |title=Billy Pritchett, RB |work=Nfl.com |date= |access-date=2019-01-08}}</ref>

Pritchett played college football for three seasons at West Texas State University, amassing 1,893 rushing yards and nine touchdowns. He had his best season as a sophomore in 1971, surpassing the 1,000-yard mark with 1,128 rushing yards and seven touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Billy Pritchett College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/billy-pritchett-1.html |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

The Cleveland Browns picked Pritchett in the 6th round of the 1974 NFL Draft. He played one season in Cleveland and two for the Atlanta Falcons. Over the course of his career Pritchett ran 280 yards and scored one rushing touchdown. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Billy Pritchett football Statistics on StatsCrew.com |url=https://www.statscrew.com/football/stats/p-pritcbil002 |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=www.statscrew.com |language=en}}</ref>

Following his football career, Pritchett worked as in the transportation industry as a freight specialist for Central Freight & Roadrunner Dawes.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Billy Pritchett, Sr. Obituary |url=https://www.chamberlandfunerals.com/obituary/Billy-PritchettSr}}</ref>

Pritchett died on March 5, 2021.<ref name=":0" />

===New York Jets===
Cashman was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the fifth round (157th overall) of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Round 5: Jets Tab Top-Tackling Minnesota LB Blake Cashman|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/round-5-jets-tab-top-tackling-minnesota-lb-blake-cashman|author=Lange, Randy|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=April 27, 2019}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on November 1, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |author=Greenberg, Ethan |title=Jets Sign LB Frankie Luvu, Place LB Blake Cashman on IR |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-lb-frankie-luvu-place-lb-blake-cashman-on-ir |website=NewYorkJets.com |date=November 1, 2019 |access-date=November 1, 2019}}</ref>

On September 15, 2020, Cashman was placed on injured reserve after suffering a groin injury in Week 1.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Place RB Le'Veon Bell, WR Denzel Mims and ILB Blake Cashman on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-rb-le-veon-bell-wr-denzel-mims-and-ilb-blake-cashman-on-injured-reser|author=Allen, Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=September 16, 2020}}</ref> He was activated on October 17.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Activate LB Blake Cashman, WR Vyncint Smith from Injured Reserve|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-activate-lb-blake-cashman-wr-vyncint-smith-from-injured-reserve|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=October 17, 2020|access-date=October 17, 2020|archive-date=October 17, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017220225/https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-activate-lb-blake-cashman-wr-vyncint-smith-from-injured-reserve|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 3, Cashman was placed back on injured reserve after suffering a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Greenberg|first=Ethan|date=December 3, 2020|title=Jets Place LB Blake Cashman on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-lb-blake-cashman-on-injured-reserve|access-date=December 2, 2020|website=New York Jets Official Website}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Goodman|first=Max|date=December 4, 2020|title=Jets Place Another Defender on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/jets/news/new-york-jets-place-linebacker-blake-cashman-on-injured-reserve|access-date=December 4, 2020|website=Jets Country}}</ref>

On September 14, 2021, Cashman was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign 4 Players; Place 4 on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-4-players-place-4-on-injured-reserve|last1=Greenberg|first1=Ethan|last2=Allen|first2=Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=September 14, 2021}}</ref> He was activated on October 9.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Activate LB Blake Cashman, Promote 2 from Practice Squad|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-activate-lb-blake-cashman-promote-2-from-practice-squad|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=October 9, 2021}}</ref> Cashman was placed back on injured reserve after suffering a groin injury in Week 7.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign S Jarrod Wilson, Release S Adrian Colbert|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-s-jarrod-wilson-release-s-adrian-colbert|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=October 26, 2021}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On March 18, 2022, Cashman was traded to the [[Houston Texans]] for a 2023 sixth-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Trade LB Blake Cashman to Texans for 2023 Sixth-Round Pick|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-trade-lb-blake-cashman-to-texans-for-2023-sixth-round-pick|author=Lange, Randy|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=March 18, 2022}}</ref> On December 2, he signed a one-year contract extension.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texans LB Blake Cashman agrees to one-year extension|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/texans/article/Texans-LB-Blake-Cashman-one-year-extension-17624348.php|author=Kubena, Brooks|website=Houston Chronicle|date=December 1, 2022}}</ref>

In Week 6 of the 2023 season, Cashman recorded 15 tackles, two for a loss, and two pass breakups in a 20–13 win over the [[New Orleans Saints]], earning [[American Football Conference]] Defensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions QB Jared Goff, Dolphins RB Raheem Mostert highlight Players of the Week|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2023-week-6-jared-goff-raheem-mostert|author=Gordon, Grant|website=NFL.com|date=October 18, 2023}}</ref> In Week 11 against the [[Arizona Cardinals]], Cashman shifted to the [[Mike linebacker]] position with [[Denzel Perryman]] suspended and [[Henry To'oTo'o]] out with a concussion. He recorded a career–high 19 tackles (13 solo), including two quarterback hits in the 21–16 victory.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Blake Cashman piles up 19 tackles in Texans' win after shifting to Mike linebacker: 'My job was to command the defense'|url=https://www.click2houston.com/sports/2023/11/20/blake-cashman-piles-up-19-tackles-in-texans-win-after-shifting-to-mike-linebacker-my-job-was-to-command-the-defense/|access-date=December 23, 2023|website=click2houston.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
On March 13, 2024, Cashman signed a three-year, $22.5 million contract with the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vikings Agree to Terms with Jonathan Greenard, Blake Cashman & Andrew Van Ginkel|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/greenard-cashman-van-ginkel-agree-to-terms-2024|website=Vikings.com|date=March 13, 2024}}</ref> He started 14 games in 2024, recording a team-leading and career-high 112 tackles, 4.5 sacks, and eight passes defensed.

Cashman began the 2025 season as one of Minnesota's starting linebackers. After suffering a hamstring injury in the team's season opener against the [[2025 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], he was placed on injured reserve on September 11, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vikings LB Blake Cashman to IR, out at least next four games|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46225933/vikings-lb-blake-cashman-ir-least-four-games|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> Cashman was activated on October 18, ahead of Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the [[2025 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vikings activate LB Blake Cashman, likely to start vs. Eagles|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46640119/vikings-activate-lb-blake-cashman-likely-start-vs-eagles|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Olabisi Johnson''' (born March 17, 1997) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Colorado State Rams football|Colorado State Rams]] and was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the seventh round of the [[2019 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Wheat Ridge, Colorado]], to Bode and Traci Johnson, Bisi played baseball and a number of other sports as a kid. He attended [[Bear Creek High School (Colorado)|Bear Creek High School]] in [[Lakewood, Colorado]], where he became a two-sport star in football and track, earning three [[varsity letters]] in both sports. He also excelled in the classroom, earning a spot on Bear Creek's Academic Athletics Honor Roll (2011–14) and was a two-time Academic All-Colorado performer (2013–14). In football, he was captain of the Bear Creek football program in 2013 and 2014. As a senior, he earned first-team All-Colorado honors after leading the Bears to a 7–4 record along with a first-round playoff victory, rushing for 698 yards with nine [[touchdowns]] and catching 25 passes for 402 yards and three more scores, racking up more than 1,500 yards of total offense running, receiving, along with returning kickoffs and punts; defensively, he led the team in tackles from his safety position with 100, including 74 solo stops. After graduating, Johnson committed to CSU over reported scholarship offers from the [[Army Black Knights football|Army]] and [[Northern Colorado Bears football|Northern Colorado]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lyell |first=Kelly |date=September 1, 2019 |title=Colorado State football's Olabisi Johnson out to prove he belongs in NFL at scouting combine |url=https://eu.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/football/2017/09/08/csu-footballs-olibisi-johnson-lives-up-nigerian-name/647117001/ |access-date=2024-03-14 |website=Coloradoan}}</ref>

Also an accomplished [[track and field]] athlete, Johnson holds the school record in the [[4 × 100 metres relay|{{nowrap|4 × 100 m}} relay]] at 42.72 seconds. At the 2014 Class 5A Colorado state meet, he won the [[110-meter hurdles]] with a time of 14.34 seconds, the [[300-meter hurdles]] with a time of 39.46 second and the pole vault (14'1" or 4.29m).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jeffco 5A League Finals - Mens Varsity 100 Meters  |url=https://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/meet/233229 |access-date=2024-03-14 |website=Athletic.net |language=en}}</ref> He was a finalist for both hurdle events as a sophomore. At the 2015 LPS Spring Break Duals, he won the [[100 meters]] with a time of 11.11 seconds.<ref>{{cite web | title=LPS Spring Break Duals | website=Athletic.net | url=https://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/meet/265351/results/m/1/100m | access-date=2025-06-07}}</ref>

==College career==
Johnson appeared in 49 career games, starting 27 for the Rams. He finished his career with 125 [[football catch|receptions]] for 2,019 yards and 11 touchdowns, being one of just 10 Rams all-time to have more than 2,000 receiving yards in a career. He set the CSU single-game record for with 265 receiving yards on a career-high 7 receptions, with 2 touchdown catches against Idaho in the [[2016 Famous Idaho Potato Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 23, 2016 |title=Olabisi Johnson sets receiving record in Potato Bowl loss |url=https://milehighsports.com/csus-olabisi-johnson-sets-receiving-record-potato-bowl-loss/ |access-date=2024-03-14 |website=Mile High Sports}}</ref>

Johnson was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the seventh round (247th overall) of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 27, 2019 |title=Vikings Select Colorado State WR Olabisi Johnson in the 7th Round of the NFL Draft |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-select-colorado-state-wr-olabisi-johnson-in-the-7th-round-of-the-nfl-dra |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

In his rookie season with the Vikings, Johnson played in all 16 games and started six of them, filling in for an injured [[Adam Thielen]]. He finished the year with a statline of 31 receptions for 294 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Olabisi Johnson 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JohnOl00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Johnson began his second season starting at receiver alongside Thielen, and in their first game of the year against the [[Green Bay Packers]], Johnson recorded 3 receptions for a career high 56 yards. However, before Week 3, rookie [[Justin Jefferson]] was named the starter over Johnson, who moved back into a reserve role.

On July 31, 2021, Johnson tore his [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]] and missed the entirety of the 2021 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schad |first=Chris |date=2021-07-31 |title=Report: Bisi Johnson tears ACL, will miss 2021 season |url=https://bringmethenews.com/minnesota-sports/report-bisi-johnson-tears-acl-will-miss-2021-season |access-date=2024-03-14 |website=Bring Me The News |language=en}}</ref>

On August 29, 2022, Johnson was placed on [[injured reserve]] after suffering a [[torn ACL]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Craig |date=August 29, 2022 |title=Vikings Place Bisi Johnson and T.Y. McGill, Jr. on Injured Reserve in Roster Moves |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/bisi-johnson-t-y-mcgill-jr-tye-smith-timon-parris-myron-mitchell-roster-moves |access-date=January 28, 2023 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Olabisi, which means "to bring prosperity to your family", is of Nigerian descent through his father, Bode Johnson, who attended college at Federal Polytechnic Ilaro in Nigeria. Bisi traveled to the African nation several times as a child to visit his grandparents, aunts and uncles and their families. Johnson received his bachelor's degree in [[Hospitality management studies|hospitality management]] from CSU in December 2018.

Brandel was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] with the 203rd overall pick in the sixth round of the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref name="fox">{{cite news |title=Vikings draft OL Blake Brandel, S Josh Metellus in sixth round |url=https://www.foxsports.com/north/story/minnesota-vikings-nfl-draft-sixth-round-blake-brandel-josh-metellus-042520 |accessdate=April 25, 2020 |work=[[Fox Sports]] |date=April 25, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the Vikings on July 27, 2020, and activated four days later.<ref>{{cite news |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/justin-jefferson-blake-brandel-brian-cole-tyler-higby-roster-moves |website=Vikings.com |date=July 27, 2020 |accessdate=July 27, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Minnesota Vikings Player Updates On Reserve/COVID-19 List |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/covid-19-players-reserve-opt-out-nfl-2020 |website=Vikings.com |date=July 31, 2020 |accessdate=August 1, 2020}}</ref> Brandel was waived by the Vikings during final roster cuts on September 5, 2020, and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Peters |first1=Craig |last2=Smith |first2=Eric |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves, Set Initial 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/2020-roster-53-man-announced |website=Minnesota Vikings |accessdate=September 5, 2020 |date=September 5, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Claim LB Ryan Connelly, Add 13 Players To Practice Squad|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/ryan-connelly-2020-practice-squad-add-13-players|website=Vikings.com|date=September 6, 2020}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Vikings on January 4, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Sign 9 Players to Reserve/Future Deals|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-sign-8-players-to-reserve-future-deals|website=Vikings.com|date=January 4, 2021}}</ref>

On September 25, 2021, Brandel was waived by the Vikings and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Sign Abdullah to 53, Elevate Dozier & Nickerson Before Home Opener|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-sign-abdullah-to-53-elevate-dozier-nickerson-before-home-opener|website=Vikings.com|date=September 25, 2021}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 18, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=October 18, 2021 |title=Vikings Place Patrick Peterson on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/patrick-peterson-ir-injured-reserve-cornerback |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

Brandel was named a backup tackle to start the 2022 season. He started three games at left tackle in place of an injured [[Christian Darrisaw]]. He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 14, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thiel |first=Sam |date=December 14, 2022 |title=Vikings Sign CB Kalon Barnes to Active Roster; Place Blake Brandel on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/kalon-barnes-signed-blake-brandel-ir-injured-roster-moves |access-date=January 8, 2024 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> He was activated on January 14, 2023.

On March 11, 2024, Brandel signed a three-year contract extension with the Vikings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Craig |date=March 11, 2024 |title=Vikings Re-Sign David Quessenberry & Blake Brandel |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/david-quessenberry-blake-brandel-re-sign-2024 |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

'''Blake Nolan Corum''' (born November 25, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] and [[kickoff returner]] for the [[Los Angeles Rams]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was a two-time [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] playing [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]], including [[unanimous All-American]] honors and the [[Big Ten Most Valuable Player]] in 2022. In [[2023 Michigan Wolverines football team|2023]], Corum became the all-time leader for the [[University of Michigan]] in rushing touchdowns with 58, set the single-season record with 27 rushing touchdowns, won three consecutive [[Big Ten Football Championship Game#Results|Big Ten Conference titles]], was a [[2024 College Football Playoff National Championship|national champion]] and earned its [[College Football Playoff National Championship#MVPs|offensive MVP award]]. He was selected by the Rams in the third round of the [[2024 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Corum was born on November 25, 2000, in [[Marshall, Virginia]],<ref name=":2" /> attending high school at [[Saint Frances Academy (Baltimore, Maryland)|Saint Frances Academy]] in [[Baltimore, Maryland]].<ref name=Bio>{{cite web|title=Blake Corum|publisher=University of Michigan|access-date=October 24, 2020|url=https://mgoblue.com/sports/football/roster/blake-corum/21973}}</ref>

He was selected as the 2019 Gatorade Player of the Year in Maryland and ''[[The Baltimore Sun]]'''s Offensive Player of the Year,<ref>{{Cite news |date=December 6, 2019 |title=St. Frances running back Blake Corum named Gatorade Maryland Football Player of the Year |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/high-school/bs-sp-digest-dec6-20191206-vimyage4fbeozdfsvyh7qaw7ku-story.html |access-date=June 8, 2024 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=2019 All-Metro football Offensive Player of the Year: Blake Corum, St. Frances|newspaper=The Baltimore Sun|page=Sports 4|date=December 19, 2019|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/61757981/blake-corum/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> rushing for 1,438 yards and 22 touchdowns during his senior season for Saint Frances as he led the Panthers to a No. 4 national ranking.<ref>{{Cite web |year=2020 |title=2019–2020 Maryland Football Player of the Year |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/blake-corum/37496 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027002942/https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/blake-corum/37496 |archive-date=October 27, 2020 |access-date=October 24, 2020 |website=Gatorade.com |publisher=Stokely-Van Camp, Inc.}}</ref> He was a four-star recruit and rated as the No. 12 high school running back.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Blake Corum – Football – University of Michigan Athletics |url=https://mgoblue.com/sports/football/roster/blake-corum/24331 |access-date=January 27, 2026 |work=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:UM UNI 09.18.21 0024 (51496797800) (2).jpg|thumb|Corum with Michigan in 2021]]

===2020 season===
Corum enrolled at the [[University of Michigan]] in January 2020.<ref name="ML20">{{Cite news |last=Zuke |first=Ryan |date=May 15, 2020 |title=Michigan OC: Freshman RB Blake Corum 'as fast as advertised' |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2020/05/michigan-oc-freshman-rb-blake-corum-as-fast-as-advertised.html |access-date=June 8, 2024 |work=[[Mlive.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Chengelis |first=Angelique S. |date=May 27, 2020 |title='Complete player' Blake Corum an explosive addition to Michigan's backfield |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2020/05/27/complete-player-blake-corum-explosive-addition-michigans-backfield/5268435002/ |access-date=June 8, 2024 |work=[[The Detroit News]]}}</ref> In his first semester at Michigan, he drew praise for both running the [[40-yard dash]] in 4.4 seconds and earning a 4.0 grade point average.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gerson |first=Aria |date=May 29, 2020 |title=Blake Corum could be Michigan's next workhorse |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/sports/football/blake-corum-could-be-michigans-next-workhorse/ |access-date=June 8, 2024 |work=The Michigan Daily}}</ref> On October 24, in the season opener versus Minnesota and his college debut, he earned his first career start. On October 31, Corum scored his first two collegiate touchdowns against rival Michigan State. As a true freshman he appeared in all six games, rushing for 77 yards (3.0 yards per carry), while also adding five receptions for 73 yards.<ref>{{cite web|title=2020 Michigan Football Statistics|publisher=University of Michigan|url=https://mgoblue.com/sports/football/stats/2020/pdf|accessdate=September 12, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Zuke |first=Ryan |date=October 7, 2020 |title=Michigan's Jay Harbaugh: Freshman RB Blake Corum will be a factor in 2020 |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2020/10/michigans-jay-harbaugh-freshman-rb-blake-corum-will-be-a-factor-in-2020.html |access-date=June 8, 2024 |work=[[Mlive.com]]}}</ref>

===2021 season===
Prior to the 2021 season, ''Sports Illustrated'' wrote that Corum was poised for a breakout year.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Brown |first=Brandon |date=August 20, 2021 |title=Blake Corum Is Destined To Be A Fan Favorite |url=https://www.si.com/college/michigan/football/blake-corum-michigan-football-mike-hart-jim-harbaugh-running-back-wolverines |access-date=June 8, 2024 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> Through the first two games of the 2021 season, Corum rushed for 282 yards on 35 carries. He averaged 141 rushing yards per game and also caught five passes for 33 yards.

Against [[2021 Washington Huskies football team|Washington]], he tallied a career high 171 rushing yards and three touchdowns, including a 67-yard touchdown run.<ref name=":2">{{cite web|title=Blake Corum|work=ESPN.com|accessdate=September 12, 2021|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/player/_/id/4429096/blake-corum|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Cohen |first=Michael |date=September 11, 2021 |title=Michigan football rolls over Washington, 31–10, behind Blake Corum and Hassan Haskins |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2021/09/11/michigan-wolverines-score-washington-huskies/8302098002/ |access-date=June 8, 2024 |work=Detroit Free Press}}</ref> He also had 128 yards on kickoff returns and led the nation in all-purpose yards with an average of 221.5 yards per game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fangman |first=Tyler |date=September 12, 2021 |title=Through 2 games, Michigan's Blake Corum leads nation in all-purpose yardage |url=https://saturdaytradition.com/michigan-football/through-2-games-michigans-blake-corum-leads-nation-in-all-purpose-yardage/ |access-date=June 8, 2024 |website=Saturday Tradition |language=en-US}}</ref>

On September 18, Corum recorded his third straight 100-yard rushing game, becoming the first Michigan player to accomplish this feat since [[Denard Robinson]] in [[2011 Michigan Wolverines football team|2011]], and the first player to record 100-plus yards rushing in three consecutive games to start the season since [[Mike Hart (American football)|Mike Hart]] in [[2007 Michigan Wolverines football team|2007]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Postgame Notes: #25 Michigan 63, Northern Illinois 10|publisher=CBS Interactive|work=MGoBlue.com|access-date=September 18, 2021|date=September 18, 2021|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/9/18/football-postgame-notes-michigan-vs-northern-illinois.aspx}}</ref>

===2022 season===
On September 17, Corum tied [[Michigan Wolverines football statistical leaders#Rushing touchdowns|Michigan's modern-era record]] with five rushing touchdowns in a game against [[2022 UConn Huskies football team|UConn]]. He became the first Michigan player to score four first-half touchdowns since [[Ed Shuttlesworth]] in [[1972 Michigan Wolverines football team|1972]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/9/17/football-michigan-blanks-uconn-behind-five-corum-rushing-tds-stifling-defense.aspx |title=Michigan Blanks UConn Behind Five Corum Rushing TDs, Stifling Defense |publisher=CBS Interactive |work=MGoBlue.com |first1=Dave |last1=Ablauf |first2=Chad |last2=Shepard |date=September 17, 2022 |access-date=September 17, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/9/17/football-postgame-notes-michigan-vs-uconn.aspx |title=Postgame Notes: #4 Michigan 59, UConn 0 |publisher=CBS Interactive |work=MGoBlue.com |date=September 17, 2022 |access-date=September 17, 2022}}</ref>

On September 24, Corum rushed for a career-high 243 yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries in a 34–27 win over [[2022 Maryland Terrapins football team|Maryland]]. His 243 rushing yards was the most for a Michigan player since [[Denard Robinson]] rushed for 258 yards in [[2010 Michigan Wolverines football team|2010]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2022/9/24/football-postgame-notes-michigan-vs-maryland.aspx|title=Postgame Notes: #4 Michigan 34, Maryland 27|publisher=CBS Interactive|work=MGoBlue.com|access-date=September 24, 2022|date=September 24, 2022}}</ref>

He continued with 133 yards against [[2022 Iowa Hawkeyes football team|Iowa]] on October 1, 124 yards against [[2022 Indiana Hoosiers football team|Indiana]] on October 8, 166 yards against [[2022 Penn State Nittany Lions football team|Penn State]] on October 15, and 177 yards against [[2022 Michigan State Spartans football team|Michigan State]] on October 29. Corum was named Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week for his performances against Maryland and Michigan State.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Iowa, Michigan and Ohio State Earn Weekly Football Honors |url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/10/31/iowa-michigan-and-ohio-state-earn-weekly-football-honors.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221031150102/https://bigten.org/news/2022/10/31/iowa-michigan-and-ohio-state-earn-weekly-football-honors.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 31, 2022 |publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=October 31, 2022 |access-date=October 31, 2022 }}</ref>

On November 19, Corum suffered a torn meniscus and sprained MCL in the first half of Michigan's game against [[2022 Illinois Fighting Illini football team|Illinois]] and played sparingly the rest of that game. Corum tried to play through the injury in the [[Michigan–Ohio State football rivalry|rivalry game]] against [[2022 Ohio State Buckeyes football team|Ohio State]] the next week. He recorded two carries for six yards on Michigan's first drive of the game but didn't play again until he took the field for a celebratory Michigan victory [[Quarterback kneel|kneel-down]] on the final play of the game.<ref>{{Citation |last=O'Donnell |first=Chris |title=Torn discoid lateral meniscus |date=May 1, 2012 |work=Radiopaedia.org |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.53347/rid-17645 |access-date=February 17, 2024 |doi=10.53347/rid-17645 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Nasr |first=Paul |date=November 21, 2023 |title=Blake Corum readies to be featured back in The Game for first time |url=http://www.michigandaily.com/sports/football/blake-corum-readies-to-be-featured-back-in-the-game-for-first-time/ |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=The Michigan Daily |language=en-US}}</ref>

At the time of his injury, Corum was a top contender for the [[Heisman Trophy]] and had the third-best odds to win it.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 13, 2022 |title=Heisman Trophy odds heading into Week 12 of college football |url=https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/2022/11/13/23455932/heisman-trophy-odds-week-12-up-cj-stroud-max-duggan-down-bo-nix-blake-corum-hendon-hooker |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=DraftKings Network |language=en}}</ref> On December 1, 2022, it was announced that Corum would undergo knee surgery,<ref>{{Cite web |last=VanHaaren |first=Tom |date=December 1, 2022 |title=Source: Michigan RB Corum to have knee surgery |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/35157349/source-michigan-rb-blake-corum-remainder-season |access-date=June 8, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> ending his season before Michigan's appearances in the [[2022 Big Ten Football Championship Game|Big Ten Championship]] and the [[College Football Playoff]] semifinal [[2022 Fiesta Bowl (December)|Fiesta Bowl]].

Over the 2022 season, Corum had 1,463 rushing yards, 18 rushing touchdowns, and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{cite web|title=2022 Michigan Football Statistics|publisher=University of Michigan|accessdate=January 14, 2023|url=https://mgoblue.com/sports/football/stats}}</ref> Corum finished seventh in voting for the Heisman Trophy,<ref>{{Cite web|last=Al-Khateeb|first=Zac|title=Who won the Heisman Trophy in 2022? Full voting results, stats, list of award winners|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-football/news/heisman-trophy-2022-winner-voting-results/aj03p9wopvjvxgcrvbisudij|access-date=January 14, 2023|website=The Sporting News|date=December 10, 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref> was named a [[unanimous All-American]] and won the [[Big Ten Most Valuable Player]], the second straight Michigan player to win MVP.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.chicagotribune.com/2022/12/15/blake-corum-is-the-2022-chicago-tribune-silver-football-winner-the-2nd-straight-michigan-player-and-19th-overall-to-win-the-98-year-old-award/|title=Blake Corum is the 2022 Chicago Tribune Silver Football winner – the 2nd straight Michigan player and the 19th overall to win the 98 year old award|work=Chicago Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Woods |first=Trevor |date=December 14, 2022 |title=Michigan RB Blake Corum named unanimous All-American |url=https://www.maizenbrew.com/football/2022/12/14/23509172/michigan-football-blake-corum-all-american |access-date=June 8, 2024 |website=Maize n Brew |language=en}}</ref>

===2023 season===
On January 9, 2023, Corum announced that he would be returning to Michigan for his senior year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Courm |first=Blake |date=January 9, 2023 |title=Corum staying at Michigan for 2023 season |url=https://twitter.com/blake_corum/status/1612526499399098368 |access-date=January 9, 2023 |website=Twitter.com}}</ref> In an appearance on the [[Rich Eisen|Rich Eisen Show]], Corum said, "I have unfinished business. I didn't like the way I went out in the Big House. I don't like people remembering me being hurt. And so I will be coming back for it all next year."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zuniga |first=Alejandro |date=January 9, 2023 |title='I'm coming back for it all': Blake Corum explains decision to return to Michigan in 2023 |url=https://247sports.com/Article/im-coming-back-for-it-all-blake-corum-explains-decision-to-return-to-michigan-in-2023-202513876/ |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=247Sports |language=en}}</ref> During halftime of a [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan basketball]] game in February, Corum spoke the crowd and guaranteed that Michigan would win the national championship in the upcoming football season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peery |first=Wade |date=February 9, 2023 |title=WATCH: Blake Corum guarantees College Football Playoff title next year during halftime vs. Nebraska basketball |url=https://www.on3.com/college/michigan-wolverines/news/watch-blake-corum-guarantees-college-football-playoff-title-next-year-during-halftime-vs-nebraska-basketball/ |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=On3 |language=en}}</ref>

On October 14, 2023, Corum had 13 carries for 52 yards, and became the tenth player in Michigan history to reach 3,000 career rushing yards. With two rushing touchdowns in the game, he passed [[Mike Hart (American football)|Mike Hart]] and [[Denard Robinson]] for the third-most career rushing touchdowns in program history (43).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/10/14/football-postgame-notes-michigan-vs-indiana |title=Postgame Notes: #2 Michigan 52, Indiana 7 |publisher=CBS Interactive |work=MGoBlue.com |access-date=October 14, 2023 |date=October 14, 2023}}</ref>

On November 4, 2023, Corum recorded three rushing touchdowns in the game, tying for second on the career rushing touchdowns list with [[Tyrone Wheatley]] at 47.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/11/4/football-postgame-notes-michigan-vs-purdue |title=Postgame Notes: #2 Michigan 41, Purdue 13 |publisher=CBS Interactive |work=MGoBlue.com |access-date=November 4, 2023 |date=November 4, 2023}}</ref>

On November 18, 2023, Corum rushed for 94 yards and two touchdowns, moving to eighth on Michigan's all-time rushing list with 3,380 yards. With his two rushing touchdowns in the game, Corum tied [[Hassan Haskins]]' single-season rushing touchdown record of 20 set in [[2021 Michigan Wolverines football team|2021]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/11/18/football-postgame-notes-michigan-at-maryland |title=Postgame Notes: #2 Michigan 31, Maryland 24 |publisher=CBS Interactive |work=MGoBlue.com |access-date=November 18, 2023 |date=November 18, 2023}}</ref>

On November 25, 2023, in the victory versus Ohio State, Corum rushed for 88 yards and two touchdowns, setting a new single-season rushing touchdown record of 22. He was the only player in the FBS to score in each game in the 2023 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/11/25/football-postgame-notes-michigan-vs-ohio-state |title=Postgame Notes: #3 Michigan 30, #2 Ohio State 24 |publisher=CBS Interactive |work=MGoBlue.com |access-date=November 25, 2023 |date=November 25, 2023}}</ref>

On December 2, 2023, in the [[2023 Big Ten Football Championship Game|Big Ten Championship]], Corum rushed for 52 yards, and two touchdowns, for his 55th career touchdown. With 52 rushing yards in the game, he passed 1,000-yards on the season, and became the first player with consecutive 1,000-yard rushing seasons since [[Denard Robinson]]. With two rushing touchdowns in the game, he tied [[Anthony Thomas (American football)|Anthony Thomas]] for Michigan's career record for rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/12/2/football-postgame-notes-michigan-vs-iowa |title=Postgame Notes: #2 Michigan 26, #18 Iowa 0 |publisher=CBS Interactive |work=MGoBlue.com |access-date=December 3, 2023 |date=December 2, 2023}}</ref>

[[File:108 MBN S23G14 ROSE (53443285154).jpg|thumb|right|Corum in the [[2024 Rose Bowl]] versus Alabama’s [[Kool-Aid McKinstry]].]]
On January 1, 2024, during the [[2024 Rose Bowl]] against [[2024 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama]], Corum rushed for 83 yards and scored two total touchdowns. He caught a receiving touchdown in the first quarter. On the second play of overtime, Corum made a jump cut and broke multiple tackles to score the game-winning touchdown to send Michigan to the national championship. In scoring his 56th career rushing touchdown, Corum broke [[Anthony Thomas (American football)|Anthony Thomas's]] previously held record to become the all-time career rushing touchdown leader at Michigan.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Knoop |first=Trent |date=January 1, 2024 |title=BREAKING: Blake Corum Is The All-Time Career Rushing Touchdown Leader At Michigan |url=https://www.si.com/college/michigan/football/blake-corum-breaks-michigan-football-all-time-rushing-touchdown-record-set-by-anthony-thomas |access-date=January 3, 2024 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref>

On January 8, Michigan played [[2023 Washington Huskies football team|Washington]] in the [[2024 College Football Playoff National Championship]] with Corum starting at running back.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Football vs Washington on 1/8/2024 – Box Score |url=https://mgoblue.com/sports/football/stats/2023/washington/boxscore/27216 |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=University of Michigan Athletics |language=en}}</ref> On the last play of the first quarter, he broke away for a 59-yard gain, the longest play of the game.<ref name=":0" /> He finished the game with 21 carries for 134 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Washington Huskies vs Michigan Wolverines – January 09, 2024 |url=https://www.foxsports.com/college-football/cfp-national-championship-washington-huskies-vs-michigan-wolverines-jan-08-2024-game-boxscore-39483 |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=FOX Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He was named [[College Football Playoff National Championship#MVPs|National Championship Offensive MVP]], finishing his senior season with 27 rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Andrew |date=January 8, 2024 |title=Michigan's Blake Corum, Will Johnson Named 2024 CFB National Championship MVPs |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10104203-michigans-blake-corum-will-johnson-named-2024-cfb-national-championship-mvps |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref>

Corum (134 yards) and [[Donovan Edwards]] (104 yards) also became the first pair of teammates in [[College Football Playoff National Championship]] history to each rush for over 100 yards.

Corum led the [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|NCAA]] with 27 rushing touchdowns, 28 total touchdowns, and 168 points scored,<ref>{{Cite web|title=2023 College Football Leaders|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/years/2023-leaders.html|website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com|access-date=November 29, 2025|language=en}}</ref> setting Michigan and Big Ten single-season records for all three. He finished his college career as Michigan's all-time leader in rushing touchdowns (58), total touchdowns (61) and points scored (366). Corum was the only [[Football Bowl Subdivision|FBS]] player in the country to score a touchdown in every one of his team's games during the 2023 season.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://mgoblue.com/sports/football/roster/blake-corum/24331|title=Blake Corum|website=University of Michigan}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Shaw |first=Zach |date=April 23, 2024 |title=NFL Draft preview: Michigan running back Blake Corum |url=https://247sports.com/college/michigan/article/nfl-draft-preview-michigan-running-back-blake-corum-230892997/ |access-date=June 8, 2024 |website=247sports.com}}</ref>

[[File:Blake Corum - Preseason 2025 Los Angeles Rams at Cleveland Browns (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|200px|Corum with the Rams in 2025]]

Corum was selected 83rd overall by the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in the third round of the [[2024 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=April 27, 2024 |title=Rams select Michigan RB Blake Corum with 83rd pick |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2024/04/26/rams-draft-blake-corum-pick-third-round-running-back/ |access-date=June 8, 2024 |website=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> In his rookie season, he played in a backup role to starting running back [[Kyren Williams]] for most of the year. Corum earned his first NFL start in Week 18 against the [[2024 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]], but suffered a season-ending fractured forearm in the game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=2025-01-07 |title=Rams place Blake Corum on injured reserve |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/rams-place-blake-corum-on-injured-reserve |access-date=January 10, 2025 |website=NBC Sports |language=en}}</ref> He finished the 2024 season with 58 carries for 207 rushing yards to go with seven receptions for 58 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Corum 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CoruBl00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=January 8, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 2025, Corum played in all 17 regular season games, growing as a complement to starter Williams. During a 33–19 victory over the [[2025 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] in Week 2, Corum scored his first career NFL touchdown on a 1-yard run in the fourth quarter. Against [[2025 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina]] in Week 13, Corum had seven carries for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Rams' 31–28 loss. A week later at [[2025 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona]], Corum had a breakout performance, rushing 12 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns, including a 48-yard TD for the longest run of his career to date. Corum added 71 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries in the Rams' 41–34 win over the [[2025 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]] in Week 15. For the regular season, Corum finished with 746 yards on six touchdowns on 145 carries (a 5.1 yards per carry average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Corum Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CoruBl00.htm |access-date=January 8, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Playing in his first-ever NFL playoff game, Corum had 11 carries for 45 yards and two receptions for 13 yards in the Rams' 34–31 wild card round victory over the [[2025 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]]. Against the [[2025 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], Corum rushed for 19 yards on six carries as L.A. won 20–17 in overtime. In the [[NFC Championship Game]] against the [[2025 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]], Corum ran nine times for 55 yards and caught three passes for 24 yards in the Rams' 31–27 loss.

During the 2026 offseason, Corum changed his jersey number from 22 to 24 to allow the newly acquired [[Trent McDuffie]] to wear the former.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=April 21, 2026 |title=Rams reveal new jersey numbers for 10 players, including Blake Corum |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/rams/2026/04/20/rams-jersey-numbers-changes-new-players-roster/89700970007/ |access-date=April 21, 2026 |website=RamsWire-USAToday.com |language=en}}</ref> Corum had previously worn No. 24 while in high school playing for [[Saint Frances Academy (Baltimore)|Saint Frances Academy]].
